About This Job
Purpose
As Technical Quotation Expert for the Component section, the successful candidate will hold a pivotal cross-over role.  The TQE will be the technical reference point within the Commercial team but liaise closely on a day-to-day basis with operational and technical colleagues, as well as with customers.  The TQE will be the primary quote-writer for the Component Test Laboratory section at UTAC's Millbrook site and other business units as required. The role will require the candidate to be responsible for technical review of RFQs, engagement with customers where additional details are required, coordination with opportunity owners and quote-writing.  In the case where a new procedure (bespoke) is requested by the customer, the TQE will be responsible for engaging with stakeholders both in the BU, commercial team and at the customer to deliver a fully priced and costed technical proposal.
The role requires technical competence, and the successful candidate will be comfortable in articulating technical quote content in a clear, concise and professional written format.  The candidate will be customer focused, responsive, and have an eye for detail and accuracy.
Responsibilities
• Technical qualification of leads
• Technical qualification of opportunities
• Interpretation of customer requirements and procedures
• Providing customer consultative guidance in determining the optimum test solution
• Providing support to the Sales organisation in attending technical customer meetings
• Collation of technical information
• Primary responsibility for preparation of technical quotations
• Primary responsibility for preparation of Statements Of Work (SOW)
• Consultation with UTAC’s Expert Network
• Providing commercial support to the Operational Project Manager
• Providing technical support to the Commercial organisation
• Supporting the achievement of sales order intake forecast within the Activity/Section of scope
• Act in accordance with the behaviours for UTAC staff at all times

Qualifications
Qualifications
• Degree level or equivalent in relevant Engineering discipline.
Experience:
• Relevant engineering experience in the field of automotive component testing (preferred)
• Sales/customer experience/mindset within an automotive or transportation setting (preferred)
Skills:
• Problem solving
• Excellent organisational and time management skills
• Able to manage own priorities without supervision
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications
• Strong verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills
• Strong organisational, analytical and problem solving skills
• Customer service/business development (advantageous)
Personal Behaviours:
• Excellent attention to detail
• Proactive in finding solutions
• Good understanding of H&S practices
• Analytical thinking
• Willingness to learn
• Methodical
• Flexible and adaptable
• Highly motivated team player
• Customer focused
• High level of confidentiality and integrity
Other:
• Full UK driving licence & own transport (UTAC is not easily assessable via public transport)
• Willing to undergo a Criminal Disclosure check
• NOTE: This position be will based at the Bedford site and will allow for some home-working, by agreement,  in line with company policies

Additional Information
For you, as a potential UTAC team member, we believe that the international and diverse nature of our business combined with the passion, energy and friendliness of our people create a great place to work. UTAC is proud to be an equal opportunities employer, valuing inclusion and supporting our people to be themselves and at their very best.
By joining us you will gain access to a broad range of learning relevant to your role and personal development, as well as exposure to leading technologies and expertise.
Our reward and benefit programmes are designed to support our people with competitive and locally tailored packages combined with support for individual health and wellbeing both inside and outside of work.

About This Job
At NEC Digital, you choose the path of no compromise. We provide industry-leading expertise across the full scope of a project, giving our customers the confidence and security they need to achieve great outcomes for users.
A partnership of best-in-class software delivery, with pioneering user-centred design services. We offer full end-to-end digital transformation expertise to the very highest standards from discovery to development and beyond, at a scale and quality unique in the market.
You must have lived in the UK for 5 consecutive years or more to be eligible for Security Clearance which is essential for the job.
We are seeking an enterprising Solution Lead to join our dynamic NEC Digital Studio team. The successful candidate will have substantial experience in designing tailored solutions for public sector clients. This role requires a hands-on approach and an understanding of the technical, non-technical and strategic aspects of solution design. It will act as the bridge between business needs, our technical/design teams and delivery, ensuring solutions are robust, compelling and aligned with NEC Digital Studio’s strategic direction.

Qualifications
Key responsibilities
• Solution ownership and design. Lead the end-to-end solution design process from early concept, and initial engagement with clients and SMEs, to delivery, ensuring alignment with client requirements and business capabilities. This role focuses not just on the technical aspect of solution design, but instead on bringing together the range of SMEs required to design and implement a relevant overarching solution.
• Internal product and capability development. Contribute to internal projects to develop new digital solutions. Lead teams to define propositions, ensuring these are technically proficient, deliverable and meet market demand.
• Pre-sales solutioning. Own and lead solution responses for RFIs, ITTs and tenders. Work closely with SMEs, sub-consultants, bid and sales teams to develop compelling, differentiating solutions.
• Leading solution workshops. Liaising with roles including: technical architects, engineering leads, support heads, business analysts and UCD SMEs, in order to formulate a full end-to-end solution for our clients. You will act as a facilitator, bringing together a full range of disciplines needed to define an integrated, robust, and scalable solution.
• Clear articulation of proposed solutions. Present and articulate solution designs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including within solution documents, presentations and solution sign-off packs.
• Client engagement. Maintain strong client relationships, understanding their needs and aligning them with feasible and innovative technological solutions.
• Continuous improvement. Keep abreast of emerging technologies, industry trends and best practices to continuously improve solution offerings and guide the technical strategy of the company.
What we need from you:
• Experience in a relevant discipline. Proven experience as a Solution Architect, Solution Lead or other relevant discipline within the IT services industry, combined with a curiosity around systems and system improvement.
• Technical expertise. Proficient in both AWS and Azure cloud platform services and solutions.
• Pre-sales experience. Experience in developing winning solutions for bids and with bid processes.
• Strong communication skills. The confidence and verbal dexterity required to lead solution workshops.
• Ability to clearly articulate solutions. To document and define proposed solution designs and create solution diagrams.
• Public sector insight. Experience working with, or for, public sector clients is highly desirable.
• Problem solver. Proven ability to analyse complex issues and, working alone or with others, design effective solutions.
Team player. Collaborative with excellent interpersonal skills and capable of working with diverse teams and clients.

Additional Information
Why Join Us?
• Impactful work. Contribute to meaningful projects that have a significant impact on public sector services.
• Innovative environment. Be a part of a new team that values innovation and encourages you to push technological boundaries.
• Professional growth. Opportunities for further development and learning to enhance your career path.
• Dynamic culture. Work in a supportive and entrepreneurial culture where your ideas are valued.
We pride ourselves in offering an excellent benefits package, including an above average pension scheme. When you join the team at NEC Software Solutions, you are provided with the following:
• Private Medical Cover funded by NEC for Employees (with the option to add family members at an additional cost)
• 25 days paid holiday with the option to buy/sell (FTE)
• 4 x basic salary life assurance cover funded by NEC (with the option to increase cover at an additional cost)
• A Group Pension Plan with fantastic employer contributions up to a maximum of 8.5%
• A selection of flexible benefits to suit your individual needs
• All colleagues get free access to LinkedIn Learning. Over 15000 courses covering a huge breadth of subjects. Learn about what you like, when you like, how you like.
OTHER INFORMATION
• Candidates must be able to demonstrate a pre-existing right to work and travel within the UK. Documentary evidence will be required.
• All offers are subject to satisfactory vetting, references and occupational health checks.
• Depending on the nature of the role a Disclosure Barring Service (DBS) check may also be required.
NEC Software Solutions is an equal opportunities employer, welcoming applications from all communities. If you require any reasonable adjustments or have specific accessibility needs during the recruitment or interview process, please feel free to share these with us. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accommodating experience for all candidates.
Who We Are:
We’re NEC Software Solutions (part of global tech giant NEC Corporation). While you read this ad, our software is helping to dispatch ambulances, support families, keep trains on the move, locate missing people and even test the hearing of newborn babies.
Working with us, you’ll be helping our 3,000+ employees push the boundaries of what’s possible and support amazing public services.
We work with governments, hospitals, police forces, housing providers, local authorities and more. We help them pay financial support faster, speed up treatments for patients and respond to emergencies in the right way. The more we do, the more our customers can do for others. And together, we make a world of difference.
We’d love your help. And we’ll support you all the way.

About This Job
As a Regulatory Data Developer, you will shape the reporting systems that keep our regulatory data accurate, timely and ready for change.
The Regulatory Data team within Data Engineering builds and maintains near real-time and batch reporting systems that support regulatory submissions and third-party reporting. This role focuses on transforming complex internal data models into regulator-ready outputs, with a strong emphasis on accuracy, traceability and performance.
You will support the migration of legacy SQL Server solutions to GCP, while helping to design and deliver new cloud-native reporting systems in BigQuery. The work spans data modelling, pipeline development, validation and automation, with AI-assisted development also playing a part in improving consistency and reducing manual effort.

Qualifications
• Strong Google BigQuery experience.
• Advanced SQL development skills, including complex queries, stored procedures and performance tuning.
• Working knowledge of GCP services such as Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions, Pub/Sub or Cloud Composer.
• Experience of building ETL or ELT data pipelines.
• Exposure to orchestration tooling for scheduled and dependency-driven workloads.
• Familiarity with SQL Server in support of legacy systems.
• Experience with Infrastructure as Code, such as Terraform.
• Exposure to CI/CD pipelines and version control tools such as Git and GitLab.
• A methodical approach with strong attention to detail.
• Interest in AI-assisted development tooling, such as Claude Code.

Additional Information
• Developing and maintaining regulatory data submission systems across on-premise SQL Server and GCP BigQuery platforms.
• Building automated pipelines for ingesting, transforming and loading regulatory data.
• Supporting the migration of legacy reporting solutions to BigQuery through data modelling and technical delivery.
• Implementing validation checks, monitoring and alerting to protect submission accuracy and reliability.
• Working with senior colleagues and technical leads to shape efficient cloud-native reporting solutions.
• Applying AI tooling and automation ideas to reduce manual effort and improve delivery quality.
• Conducting QA to confirm solutions are accurate, performant and aligned to regulatory requirements.
• Producing and maintaining clear documentation for technical processes and solution designs.
• Participating in code reviews and following departmental development standards.
• Collaborating with colleagues to deliver high-quality work within required timeframes.

You could be joining our award-winning, small, family-run, local home care company who's visits always involve an element of companionship. We have won multiple awards over the years and have built an excellent reputation in the local area. This home care service with the personal touch is different to any other care organisation in the area, providing a minimum of 1-hour home visits to a predominantly private client base, but the focus being on companionship and loneliness prevention. The average visiting time is actually far higher at about 90 minutes and our friendly office team are sensible about travel time and distances as well so you'll be visiting clients within a pre-agreed area to suit you.
There are some fantastic benefits & hours too in your role as Care Companion & Elderly Befriender, including:

·        The biggest benefit of all is making a difference every day and putting a smile on your clients faces
Help us in our mission to end loneliness amongst our local elderly population

·        Shopping tips, social Calls, appointments, clubs & hobbies (own car advantageous)

Driving Licence and access to vehicle essential.

• Ability to travel up to 50 percent of the time, including international if necessary

Recruiting for positions in Norfolk
CQC Outstanding Home Instead Senior Care are recruiting for live in carers to work with their clients in Norfolk, UK.
Please are looking to recruit caring, compassionate individuals who are passionate about making a difference to our clients.
Our live in Caregivers are supporting with local support and guidance.
Home Instead Senior Care Live In CAREGiver Job Description
Objective
To live in a client’s home and provide a variety of non-medical services that enhance the quality of their life. To help clients and their families meet the challenges of aging with dignity, pride, care and compassion.
Primary Responsibilities:
• Provide live in care, usually working alone
• Reflect the core values of Home Instead Senior Care franchise
• Contribute to a positive living environment to enhance a client’s quality of life
• As you will be staying in the client’s home, you will follow their house rules and be mindful of their need for privacy
• You may be the only person the client sees over a period of time, it is therefore essential to document daily activities and report any changes or causes for concern in a client’s needs or living conditions
• You need to be clear about when to seek help and advice to keep clients safe and promote their well-being
• Maintain regular communication with line manager and office staff
COMPANIONSHIP services which could include, but are not limited to:
• Offer companionship and conversation
• Monitor diet and eating
• Stimulate and encourage through a variety of activities (for example clothing selection, hobbies and crafts)
• Arrange and provide reminders for appointments, activities and outings
• Help with travel arrangements
• Organise mail and write letters
• Assist with walking (lending an arm to steady)
• Accompany to appointments and social events (for example visiting friends or family, lunch, club meetings)
HOME HELP services which could include, but are not limited to:
• Run errands / collect prescriptions etc
• Performing light housekeeping tasks (dusting, vacuuming, making beds, changing linens, cleaning bathrooms, kitchens, washing and ironing, taking out rubbish, caring for houseplants etc.)
• Organise and tidy cupboards and check food expiry dates
• Plan prepare and tidy away meals
• Answer the door
• Assist with pet care
• Supervise home maintenance
• Help with shopping and oversee home deliveries
PERSONAL CARE services which could include, but are not limited to:
• Provide medication reminders
• Help with bathing, dressing and grooming
• Help with continence care
• Assist to eat and drink
• Provide Dementia / Alzheimer care
• Provide respite / convalescence care
• Assist with morning/wake up and or evening/tuck in
Secondary Responsibilities:
• Participate in company sponsored training and social events including CAREGiver meetings
• Report hours according to office policy & communicate changes in availability in a timely manner
• Participate in PEAQ engagement Survey
• Document client information in Client and Life Journal
• May require you to run errands and provide incidental transportation for a client using your vehicle or a client’s vehicle
• Perform other reasonable duties as assigned
Essential Criteria:
• Ability to treat and care for clients and their property with dignity and respect
• Ability to adapt to various living environments and locations
• Ability to listen, communicate clearly and build relationships with clients and their families in a friendly and pleasant manner
• Willingness to work and communicate professionally with Home Instead Senior Care office teams and other social and health care professionals
• Respect for people suffering from a range of medical conditions with different backgrounds and beliefs to your own. Commitment to non-discriminatory care practice
• Willing to seek guidance when needed and follow instructions
• Excellent time keeper who is organised and reliable
• Ability to adapt to change quickly and make common sense decisions at short notice
• Good hygiene practice, including personal hygiene and a smart appearance
• Good level of stamina and fitness to meet the physical demands of the job
• This role will require you to obtain an Enhanced Disclosure from the relevant body
• Class 1 business insurance (if using own car for business purposes)

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001550.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Build and operate the interface, semantic layer and controls that let AI agents work inside IFS software safely.
This role is hybrid or remote.
The role:
You will own the web client of an AI agent product for our enterprise customers. It is a React and TypeScript single-page application, and almost everything on its screen arrives as a stream from a language-model agent.
What you will do:
• Build an interface that people can trust while the content on it is still arriving, changing and occasionally wrong.
• Turn what the agent produces into a usable interface: prose, generated views and actions the user can take.
• Make sure the agent acts only with the user's explicit consent, and that people can always see what it did and why.
• Own the front-end architecture, the component system and the contracts with the teams behind the agent.
• Help move the interface towards Lit and Web Components, so that what we build is standards-based and not tied to a single framework or application.
• Treat accessibility, performance, testing and observability as part of the product rather than a late pass.
• Work across the boundary into the services your interface depends on, then ship what you build and run it in production.
Why it is interesting:
Most front-end work assumes that a page loads and is then correct. Here the content arrives in pieces, gets revised, sometimes fails partway and is sometimes wrong. And some of it is code a model wrote, which the browser should not trust. The protocols involved are young and still changing (AG-UI, A2UI, MCP Apps). You will help shape them, not just consume them.
What we are looking for:
• Substantial production single-page applications, built and operated, with real depth in TypeScript and React.
• Asynchronous state you can reason about.
• Browser security as a working concern: iframe sandboxing, postMessage, Content Security Policy, sanitising content you did not write.
• Component and design-system work in a shared codebase, including web components used inside React.
• Accessibility as a practice. You know how to keep it tested.
• Willing to write Go and to read Python. Prior experience in either is not required.
• Test-first habits and continuous delivery.
• Clear writing. Decisions are recorded as short architecture decision records (ADRs), and protocols are documented before they change.
• Comfortable working with AI coding agents as part of how you build.
Also valuable:
• A product surface built on a language model in production: streaming, partial output, retries, and showing uncertainty.
• Hands-on knowledge of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and MCP Apps, AG-UI or A2UI.
• Experience building with Lit and Web Components, including shadow DOM and custom elements used from other frameworks.
• Expression languages or compilers.
• A platform where behaviour is configured through data or metadata rather than written in code.
• Data visualisation.
• Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes and Helm.
• Knowledge of an enterprise domain: asset management, field service, manufacturing, supply chain.

Qualifications
•
Production experience building and operating substantial single-page applications, with real depth in modern TypeScript and a current framework such as Angular or React.
•
Built a product surface on top of a language model in production: streaming, partial output, cancellation, retries, and what to show when the system is uncertain.
•
Component architecture and design-system work in a codebase other teams contribute to.
•
Accessibility as a working practice, and performance work you can describe in numbers.
•
Comfortable across the boundary: you can write the service-side code your surface needs.
•
Automated testing, observability and continuous delivery as part of how you build.
Also valuable
•
A platform where behaviour is configured through data or metadata rather than written in code.
•
Mobile or progressive web applications, including offline behaviour and poor connectivity.
•
Voice interfaces.
•
Enterprise software domains: asset management, field service, manufacturing, supply chain.

Additional Information
We believe that coming together as a community, in person, is important for innovation, connection and fostering a sense of belonging. Our roles have the right balance of remote and in-office working to enable flexibility for managing your life along with ensuring a real connection with your colleagues and the broader IFS community.

About This Job
We are looking for MSAT team member who will serve as the technical bridge between process development and commercial production. Operating within a cGMP environment, this role provides end-to-end technical oversight, process engineering expertise, and scientific support to ensure the robust, scalable, and safe manufacture of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). The successful candidate will drive technology transfers, lead complex root-cause investigations, and champion continuous process improvement (CPI) to optimize product yield and quality.
Responsibilities:
1. Technology Transfer & Scale-Up
• Support the technical transfer of new API / Intermediate chemical synthesis processes from MSAT lab or external customers into commercial-scale manufacturing.
• Conduct laboratory experiments for feasibility studies and / or continuous improvement purpose.
• Perform facility-fit assessments, chemical engineering calculations (e.g., mass/energy balances, heat transfer, mixing dynamics), and scale-up modeling.
• Draft, review, and execute Technology Transfer Protocols, Campaign Summary Reports, and regular technical risk assessments (FMEA).
• Support to the EHS department in analysis the process safety data and interpretation.
2. Process Validation & Monitoring
• Support to the Validation program Process / clean protocols and Continued Process Verification (CPV) plans in alignment with ICH guidelines and Quality compliance requirements.
• Provide real-time shop floor technical support during active manufacturing campaigns and validation batches.
3. Deviation, Investigation & CAPA Management
• Act as the Technical Subject Matter Expert (SME) for manufacturing deviations, batch failures, and out-of-specification (OOS) results.
• Utilize structured root-cause analysis (RCA) tools (e.g., Fishbone, 5 Whys) to determine technical root causes and implement robust Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs).
4. Continuous Improvement & Lifecycle Management
• Identify and implement process optimization initiatives to enhance yield, minimize impurity profiles, reduce solvent consumption, and cut cycle times.
• Manage technical aspects of lifecycle changes, authoring technical justifications for change controls.
5. Regulatory & Compliance Support
• Support the technical queries for regulatory filing queries.
• Participate as a technical SME during regulatory inspections and client audits.

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related technical discipline
Experience:
Minimum 5 Years of experience in pharmaceutical industry.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/sectigo/3743990.description_excerpt:
About This Job
We are looking for a hands-on PostgreSQL DBA to help manage database services across our on-premises infrastructure and GCP. The role combines production operations with project work, including migration from Community PostgreSQL to EDB Postgres, high-availability standardization, database consolidation, and operational automation.
You will work closely with DBAs, SRE, infrastructure, application, and security teams. We need someone who can assess the current environment, identify risks and improvements, recommend practical solutions, and follow them through to stable production operations.
Here are the core functions, responsibilities, and expectations for this role:
• PostgreSQL and EDB administration. Administer the full database lifecycle, including installation, configuration, patching, upgrades, capacity planning, security, monitoring, incident response, and decommissioning.
• High availability with EFM. Configure, operate, monitor, and troubleshoot EDB Failover Manager clusters; perform planned switchovers and failover tests; validate application connectivity; and safely reintegrate failed or former primary nodes.
• Backup and recovery with Barman. Configure and monitor base backups and WAL archiving or streaming, manage retention, execute point-in-time recovery, and conduct documented restore and disaster-recovery tests against agreed RPO and RTO targets.
• Monitoring and alerting with PEM. Register and manage servers and agents, configure meaningful metrics and alert thresholds, investigate alerts and performance trends using graphs, and maintain notification and escalation integrations.
• Automation and version control. Use TPA and Ansible/Spacelift to build repeatable PostgreSQL/EDB environments and maintain playbooks and configuration in Git and GitHub using branches, pull requests, and peer review.
• Replication and recovery. Configure and troubleshoot physical streaming and logical replication, replication slots, WAL retention, lag, and timeline issues; use pg_rewind when appropriate to resynchronize a node after timelines diverge.
• Performance engineering. Analyze execution plans and wait or lock behavior, tune SQL and indexes, and optimize PostgreSQL and operating-system settings, including autovacuum, memory, storage, and checkpoint or WAL behavior.
• Connectivity and security. Operate PgBouncer and manage roles, privileges, authentication, pg_hba.conf, TLS, secrets, and least-privilege access in line with organizational standards.
• Migrations and consolidation. Plan and execute major and minor version upgrades, Community PostgreSQL-to-EDB migrations, and database consolidation with validated rollback, testing, and minimal downtime.
• Operational ownership. Create runbooks and architecture documentation, participate in change and incident processes, collaborate with engineering teams, and join an on-call rotation for production emergencies.
• Additional tasks associated with this position may be assigned in response to company initiatives and business needs.
More information about this role:
This is a full-time and remote position based in the U.K. The target compensation package for this role is between GBP 50,000 and 54,000, subject upon internal equity and years of experience.  We may make further adjustments through an approval process if the targeted compensation range needs to be modified based on business needs and market trends.

Qualifications
Education:
• Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer science, technology, or a related field is strongly preferred. In lieu of degree, 2+ years of relevant and/or equivalent experience is acceptable.
Experience:
• Minimum of 5+ years of hands-on PostgreSQL administration in production environments, including both routine operations and complex troubleshooting is required.
• Hands-on production experience with EDB Postgres, EFM, Barman, PEM, and TPA, along with PostgreSQL monitoring using Prometheus and Grafana.
• Strong understanding of PostgreSQL HA design, streaming replication, failure detection, switchovers, failovers, quorum or witness concepts, split-brain prevention, and node rejoin procedures.
• Demonstrated experience with backup validation, WAL archiving, retention management, point-in-time recovery, and full restore or disaster-recovery testing.
• Strong knowledge of PostgreSQL internals, including WAL, MVCC, vacuum and autovacuum, checkpoints, memory management, locking, and transaction behavior.
• Strong SQL performance-tuning skills, including EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), index design, query-plan analysis, and diagnosis of blocking or resource contention.
• Solid Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including CPU, memory, filesystem, storage I/O, systemd services, networking, and shell scripting.
• Strong hands-on experience with Ansible, Git, and GitHub, including playbooks, inventories, pull requests, peer review, conflict resolution, and version-controlled TPA configuration.
• Hands-on experience configuring, administering, and troubleshooting PgBouncer.
• Experience with GCP and/or AWS, including virtual machines, networking, storage, identity and access management, and cloud monitoring.
• Clear written and verbal communication, disciplined documentation, sound production judgment, and willingness to participate in an on-call rotation.
Ideal Candidate Profiles, Talents, and Desired Qualifications:
• Experience with comparable PostgreSQL tools such as Patroni, repmgr, pgBackRest, or pgWatch.
• Experience with Terraform and automation using Bash or Python.
• Previous involvement in large PostgreSQL migrations, major-version upgrades, database consolidation, or hybrid on-premises/cloud environments.
• Experience administering MariaDB or MySQL.
• You are a practical, accountable DBA who balances availability and data protection with delivery needs. You investigate carefully, communicate risk clearly, automate repeatable work, test recovery procedures rather than assuming they work, and remain calm during production incidents.

Additional Information

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws in the countries where we operate.

• This is not an INTERNAL SOC ROLE.
• The Ideal candidate will bring a mixture of technical and strong client/stakeholder management.
• The role could include supporting clients in enhancing their SecOps environments to providing hands on active support.
• The candidate should feel comfortable in fast paced environments and client environments.
You will combine hands-on operational leadership with advisory work. This means managing live incident containment and day-to-day SOC operations, while helping enterprise and public sector clients modernise their security operations, improve their SIEM, SOAR and EDR capabilities, and build stronger cyber resilience.
Why consider joining our Digital & Data community? 🤔
• Join our Digital & Data team and work alongside cyber security, product, design and technology specialists in cross-disciplinary teams to solve complex client challenges and bring ideas to life.
• Build a flexible and distinctive career in a trust-based, inclusive environment that values excellence, innovation and curiosity. You can progress through a technical career track without needing to follow the Partner career track if that does not align with your ambitions.
• Work across a broad range of Security Operations engagements, client environments and technology stacks spanning seven sectors. No two projects are the same.
• Join a supportive and collaborative cyber and technology community, with knowledge sharing, peer support, coaching and mentoring from other specialists.
• Deepen your expertise through our culture of learning and growth, with access to a development budget for technical and non-technical training and professional certifications.
• Benefit from a hybrid working approach, with an expectation of being in the office or on a client site for a minimum of two days per week, depending on the role and assignment.
What you'll do 🌱
• Lead and develop SOC analysts and incident response specialists, providing clear operational direction, coaching and support across day-to-day security operations.
• Take a hands-on leadership role during cyber security incidents, coordinating investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, stakeholder communications and post-incident reviews.
• Help enterprise and public sector clients assess and improve their Security Operations capabilities, identifying gaps across people, processes and technology and translating these into practical improvements.
• Advise on the evolution and optimisation of SIEM, SOAR, EDR and threat-detection tooling to improve visibility, reduce noise and strengthen detection and response capabilities.
• Develop and maintain incident playbooks, standard operating procedures, automated response workflows and proactive tabletop exercises.
• Support the development of modern Security Operations services and ways of working, sharing your expertise across our Digital Trust & Cyber Security community through coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing.
Security technologies you'll work with 🚀
We advocate using the right technology for the right task. Depending on the client environment and engagement, you can expect to work across technologies including:
• SIEM and security analytics platforms, such as Microsoft Sentinel and Splunk.
• SOAR and security automation technologies used for enrichment, triage and response orchestration.
• Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR/XDR) platforms, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and CrowdStrike Falcon.
• Threat intelligence, detection engineering, investigation and incident response technologies.
• Cloud security monitoring across Microsoft Azure, AWS and GCP environments.
What you can expect 🌱
• Work collaboratively across multiple technical teams and stakeholder groups, using your Security Operations expertise to solve complex client problems and contribute to internal initiatives.
• Participate in live, in-person working sessions to investigate incidents, assess operational challenges and design practical improvements, alongside asynchronous collaboration through Microsoft Teams.
• Work with the team at client sites or in our offices for a minimum of two days per week. The time you spend and where you work will vary by role and assignment, including the possibility of being on a client site for up to five days per week.
• Work in an environment that takes its values seriously and places collaboration, inclusion, learning and client impact at the heart of how teams operate.

Qualifications
Essential requirements ✅
Even if you don’t meet every requirement below, feel free to still apply as we are often hiring for similar roles which your background might be better suited to.
• SOC Leadership: Experience running or supervising a SOC, CSOC, or Incident Response team.
• Incident Response: Practical experience managing live cyber incidents (such as ransomware, account takeovers, or supply chain breaches).
• Technical Stack: Direct experience working with major SIEM/SOAR tools (e.g., Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk) and EDR/XDR platforms (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon).
• Security Frameworks: Solid understanding of MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, NCSC Caf v4.0 and ISO 27001.
• Communication: Ability to write concise incident reports and speak comfortably with both engineers and business leaders.
Desirable
• Experience working in management consulting, managed services (MSSP), or client-facing advisory roles.
• Experience in regulated UK environments (such as Central Government,  Defence, or Critical National Infrastructure).
• Hands-on familiarity with cloud security monitoring in AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Please be aware that some of our UK roles at PA Consulting require a UK security clearance.
All PA people are required to undergo background checks and to achieve the Baseline Personnel Security Standard however, some UK roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting, where applicants must have at least 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.
We therefore ask that you only apply if you meet the residency requirements (i.e. you are a British citizen or have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years), as this is the prerequisite for a security clearance. If you're unsure about your eligibility, we encourage you to review the UK Government’s guidance on security vetting before applying.

Additional Information
Assessment process ⚖️

The Senior Automation Developer will play a key role in delivering intelligent automation solutions across both Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust and Isle of Wight NHS Trust.
You will design, develop, test, and support Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Power Platform applications, applying your technical expertise to streamline business processes, enhance digital capabilities, and support the Trusts’ wider digital transformation strategies.

About This Job
We are seeking a Data Scientist to design and deliver analytical models and decision-support systems that improve understanding, prediction and decision-making across the business.
The role focuses on building practical models of complex real-world systems, working with imperfect data, uncertainty and competing objectives to generate commercially valuable outcomes.
Responsible for developing deployable analytical solutions in partnership with Engineering teams, while not owning production infrastructure or application development.
Key Responsibilities:
Model Development
• Design, develop and maintain statistical, probabilistic and simulation-based models.
• Translate complex business questions into tractable modelling problems.
• Select appropriate modelling approaches based on the characteristics of the problem rather than methodological preference.
• Develop prototypes and working solutions iteratively, refining approaches as new information becomes available.
• Build analytical assets that can be reused as products, decision-support tools or operational capabilities.
• Design and analyse experiments to evaluate interventions, operational changes and model effectiveness.
Inference & Uncertainty
• Work effectively with incomplete, imperfect and evolving datasets.
• Develop approaches for estimating missing information and combining evidence from multiple sources.
• Quantify uncertainty and communicate appropriate confidence in model outputs.
• Test assumptions and identify limitations within modelling approaches.
Optimisation & Decision Support
• Develop frameworks that improve operational and commercial decision-making.
• Evaluate alternative actions, trade-offs and potential outcomes.
• Support automation of appropriate decision processes through analytical models.
• Design experiments and simulations that inform strategic and operational choices.
Validation & Quality
• Validate models using appropriate testing, back-testing and comparison techniques.
• Assess sensitivity to assumptions and changing conditions.
• Monitor model performance over time and identify concept drift or degradation.
• Maintain high standards of analytical rigour and reproducibility.
Collaboration & Communication
• Partner closely with Business Analysts, Engineering, Product and operational teams.
• Explain modelling approaches, assumptions and results clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Document methodologies, limitations and recommendations in a practical and accessible way.
• Contribute to a culture of experimentation and evidence-based decision-making.
Productisation & Engineering Partnership
• Design models and analytical approaches with operational deployment in mind.
• Work closely with Engineering teams to translate models into scalable production solutions – Data Science defines the models while Engineering owns production implementation.
• Define model inputs, outputs, assumptions and performance requirements required for implementation.
• Support the development of APIs, services or analytical components by providing technical guidance and validation.
• Contribute to testing and acceptance of implemented solutions to ensure behaviour aligns with model expectations.
• Help define monitoring, evaluation and retraining requirements where appropriate.
• Partner with Product, Engineering and Business teams to ensure analytical solutions deliver measurable business value.

Qualifications
Essential
• Strong grounding in applied statistics, modelling, data science, operational research, economics, mathematics or a related quantitative discipline.
• Experience building models that support real-world decisions, products or operational processes.
• Experience working with uncertainty, incomplete information and imperfect datasets.
• Ability to move from loosely defined problems to practical analytical solutions.
• Strong problem decomposition and structured thinking skills.
• Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
• Strong coding skills in Python or R.
• Experience developing analytical solutions in code rather than primarily through spreadsheet-based analysis.
• Experience taking analytical models from prototype through to operational deployment.
Core Technical Skills
Candidates should demonstrate strength in several of the following areas:
• Statistical modelling
• Probabilistic modelling
• Bayesian inference
• Forecasting
• Machine learning
• Simulation modelling
• Agent-based modelling
• Optimisation techniques
• Experimental design
• Synthetic data generation
• Decision science
• Scenario analysis
As important as experience with any individual technique is the ability to understand trade-offs and select the most appropriate approach for the problem being solved.
Experience or familiarity with the following is desirable
• Building simulation or digital twin style systems.
• Optimisation, operational research or decision science techniques.
• Working with survey, panel or market research data.
• Applying machine learning or AI techniques to business problems.
• Model monitoring, governance and validation practices.
• Contributing to analytical products rather than one-off analyses.
• Modern AI and generative AI approaches.
• Working in multidisciplinary teams alongside software engineers and product teams.
• Software development lifecycles and productionisation of analytical solutions.
• Defining requirements and acceptance criteria for model implementation

Additional Information
Employee Benefits:

• Participation in a company bonus scheme linked to personal and company performance
• Group Life Cover 4x salary
• Pension 4%/4% employee/employer contributions
• Vitality after probation
• Staff discount scheme

About This Job
The role
This is an opportunity to join our global Knowledge and Training (K&T) function as a Knowledge Lawyer supporting our global fintech practice, with a focus on regulatory developments in the UK and EU.
Clifford Chance is one of the world's leading law firms. Clifford Chance's vision is to be one of the elite global law firms and we aim to achieve this through a focus on client service excellence. The K&T function drives quality, consistency, efficiency, and innovation across Clifford Chance, producing better-trained fee earners, supported by gold-standard knowledge resources. We use tools that leverage firm-wide knowledge and artificial intelligence (AI) to create competitive advantage through smarter, more complex, more accurate and more efficient legal work.
Clifford Chance’s fintech practice is recognised as a global leader, guiding clients through some of the most innovative and complex transactions in the market, including those involving distributed ledger technology (DLT) infrastructure, cryptoassets, pioneering payments solutions and AI. Our client base is as diverse as it is distinguished, including major international financial institutions, market infrastructure providers and asset managers alongside leading fintechs and cryptoasset service providers, corporates, regulators and policy makers.
Who you will work with
You will deliver practical and insightful knowhow and advice to Partners and lawyers focussed on fintech matters to help them provide a high quality and cost effective service to our clients.
While you will work with lawyers across the firm's Product Groups, you will sit within our leading Financial Regulation team, which is part of our wider Capital Markets Global Product Group. The London team you will sit with is ranked as Tier 1 for Fintech: regulatory in Legal 500.
As part of our global K&T function, you will work collaboratively with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists across our global network. In particular, you will work closely with the Knowledge and Information Officer for Fintech and with the rest of our global Tech Group Knowledge team, currently made up of the global lead for Tech knowledge, three other Knowledge Lawyers and another information officer specialising in wider tech work. You will work alongside the global lead for Tech knowledge to coordinate efforts on strategy, knowledge and thought leadership.
You will also work closely with our Thought Leadership function, Business Development, Marketing and Communications, PR and other business professional teams – for example on the preparation of briefings, template pitch materials and client training materials, supporting media outreach and in relation to knowledge and marketing campaigns. Work on innovation and AI projects will also bring the opportunity to work with Clifford Chance's Transformation team and Legal Technology Advisors who work collaboratively with fee earners and Knowledge Lawyers to deliver the highest-quality, efficient and cost-effective client service.
The role also includes engagement with external stakeholders. For example, there are often opportunities to support client outreach and training, while policy and trade association work provides opportunities to interact with clients, regulators such as the Financial Conduct Authority, trade bodies and peers at other law firms.
What you will be responsible for
Fintech legal and regulatory expertise and knowledge management
• Monitoring and analysing fintech legal and regulatory developments in order to update lawyers and clients on their impact, for example including around the regulation of cryptoassets, stablecoins, tokenised deposits, payments and AI. You will have a particular focus on UK and EU developments with an awareness of relevant international developments.
• Responding to fintech and digital assets regulatory queries from lawyers and teams across the firm’s network and providing ad hoc fintech input into wider internal knowledge resources.
• Supervising and providing strategic input into internal and client-facing fintech resources managed by a Knowledge and Information Officer, including fintech topic guides and regular fintech and cryptoasset horizon-scanning newsletters.
• Identifying opportunities to improve the capture, organisation and sharing of fintech knowhow across the firm, including the potential development of new curated knowledge collections, practice notes, templates and/or clause libraries.
• Encouraging and engaging with fee earners to share and submit knowhow to the firm's knowledge database.
Thought leadership and client publications
• Preparing and supporting client briefings, blog posts, webinars and other client-facing materials on market trends and regulatory developments, including supporting relevant external journal and publication opportunities.
• Leading or contributing to thought leadership publications on key fintech topics, including an annual fintech trends publication, as well as contributions to broader publications requiring fintech input.
Trade association and policy work
• Drafting, coordinating and contributing to consultation responses and policy submissions on fintech and digital assets regulation.
• Participating in relevant working groups of trade associations, external committees and Knowledge Lawyer community discussions, and supporting partners and colleagues in doing the same.
Business planning and strategic client development
• Working alongside the relevant business development leads and key partners and counsel on fintech business planning, including helping to identify strategic priorities, themes and target clients in line with the firm’s wider strategy and K&T priorities.
• Reviewing and contributing to fintech capability statements, marketing materials and providing input into strategic client panels, pitches and other client development materials.
• Preparing bespoke materials to support targeted client outreach on identified themes and supporting client-facing training, including the preparation of client training decks.
Training
• Preparing and delivering regular internal training on key fintech developments, including UK and EU cryptoasset regulatory developments.
• Coordination, support and/or delivery of internal global fintech training as part of the Tech Group training programme.
• Supporting client and internal training initiatives by identifying relevant themes, preparing materials and coordinating input from subject matter experts.
AI, legal technology and innovation
• Supporting the development, adoption and effective use of legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, across the London office and globally, including helping to identify appropriate use cases to improve matter delivery and lawyer productivity, share best practice, and embed new ways of working.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/averna1/7440001.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The Role
We are looking for a practical, technically capable and highly customer-focused Customer Support Technician to become our primary day-to-day representative at a major customer site near Cheltenham.
This is much more than a traditional maintenance or technician role. You will be embedded within the customer's operation and will develop a detailed understanding of their test systems, equipment and day-to-day challenges. You will provide first-line technical support, undertake hands-on electrical and mechanical work and act as the link between the customer and Averna's wider engineering organisation.
You will not be expected to know the answer to every problem yourself. An important part of the role is having the technical judgement to investigate issues effectively, recognise when additional expertise is required and engage the appropriate specialists from across Averna.
Just as importantly, you will build relationships across the customer's organisation. Working closely with our Account Manager and engineering teams, you will help us identify where equipment, processes or support could be improved and turn those observations into potential engineering solutions and new opportunities.
For the right person, this is an opportunity to become a trusted technical partner to the customer rather than simply somebody who repairs equipment when it fails.
Key Responsibilities
Customer and Technical Support
• Act as Averna's primary day-to-day representative at the customer site and build strong working relationships with engineering, production, maintenance and other customer teams.
• Provide first-line support for test systems and associated equipment including both Averna-supplied systems and equipment originally supplied by others.
• Investigate faults and operational issues and establish the appropriate course of action.
• Diagnose faults to module level and, where appropriate, component level using standard electronic test equipment.
• Work closely with Averna engineering specialists to escalate more complex problems and bring the appropriate expertise to bear.
• Develop a strong working knowledge of the customer's equipment, systems and operating environment.
• Help identify recurring issues, weaknesses and opportunities to improve equipment reliability, maintainability, usability and performance.
• Provide a responsive and pragmatic service while recognising the limits of your own knowledge and seeking specialist support where appropriate.
Hands-on Engineering
• Undertake electrical wiring, modification, repair and rework activities in accordance with customer requirements and approved engineering information.
• Carry out wiring, looming, crimping, terminating and soldering activities to an appropriate professional standard.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring schedules, general arrangement drawings and other engineering documentation.
• Follow calibration, test and diagnostic procedures accurately and use the results to identify potential equipment failures.
• Use standard instrumentation including DMMs, oscilloscopes and LCR meters to support fault diagnosis.
• Undertake basic mechanical and fabrication activities associated with test equipment including drilling, panel modification, removal of damaged fasteners and thread repair.
• Work with the customer and Averna engineering teams where modifications or repairs require additional design authority, specialist knowledge or engineering approval.
Customer Development
• Work closely with the Averna Account Manager to understand the customer's wider objectives, priorities and challenges.
• Identify opportunities where Averna's engineering, test, support or obsolescence capabilities could improve the customer's operation.
• Recognise potential requirements arising from recurring faults, ageing equipment, capacity constraints, process inefficiencies or new programmes.
• Help engineering and sales colleagues understand and develop these opportunities by providing practical insight from the customer environment.
• Support site visits, technical discussions and requirements capture activities where appropriate.
• Contribute to making Averna easier to work with and continually improving the customer's experience of our business.
Wider Field Support
Although the role will be predominantly based at the customer site near Cheltenham, there may occasionally be a requirement to support Averna test systems installed at other customer locations.
This may include:
• Supporting ATEC and other test systems at customer sites elsewhere in the UK.
• Occasional travel to European customer locations.
• Working closely with engineering and support colleagues in France and elsewhere within the Averna Group.
• Occasional travel to Toulouse for technical training, knowledge transfer and team activities.
• Occasional visits to Averna's UK operation, currently based in Bournemouth.
The Cheltenham customer site will remain the principal place of work and travel is expected to represent a relatively small proportion of the role.
About You
Technical capability is important but personality, judgement and customer skills are equally important to this position. You will be comfortable working independently within a customer's organisation and will naturally build relationships with the people around you. You will be curious about how things work and why problems occur rather than simply addressing the immediate symptom. You will have the confidence to take ownership of problems while also having the judgement to recognise when you need help. Averna has considerable engineering expertise available across the wider organisation and we want someone who will make effective use of that expertise rather than feeling they have to solve everything alone.
You will ideally be:
• Outgoing, approachable and comfortable dealing with people at different levels within a customer organisation.
• A good communicator and conversationalist who naturally develops strong working relationships.
• Practical and hands-on with a strong problem-solving mentality.
• Able to work independently and use your own initiative.
• Sensible and pragmatic with good technical judgement and common sense.
• Curious and willing to investigate problems rather than simply follow instructions.
• Confident enough to take ownership but self-aware enough to recognise when specialist expertise is required.
• Customer-focused and motivated by finding better ways of doing things.
• Commercially aware and able to recognise when a technical issue or customer challenge could represent a wider opportunity.
• Comfortable working collaboratively with engineering and sales colleagues across different locations and countries.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role will mean that the customer sees you as their first point of contact when they have a test equipment problem or need help finding a better way of doing something.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/scalian/7440001.description_excerpt:
About This Job
We are looking for experienced Configuration Managers to join an engineering team in Pitstone.
The team is looking for two Configuration Managers with around 5+ years' experience and one Senior/Lead Configuration Manager with significant Configuration Management experience.
The role will be responsible for effective Configuration Management across complex engineering projects, maintaining configuration baselines, controlling engineering changes, and ensuring accurate and traceable product information throughout the product lifecycle.
The team has recently migrated to a Windchill PLM environment, creating a strong focus on data quality, configuration governance, product structures, and the alignment of engineering information across PLM, ERP, drawings and BOMs.
Key Responsibilities:
• Develop and maintain Configuration Management Plans for new and existing projects.
• Provide Configuration Management guidance to project and engineering teams.
• Define and maintain Configuration Items (CIs), product structures and Bills of Materials (BOMs).
• Establish and maintain configuration baselines, including Functional, Allocated and Product Baselines.
• Manage configuration identification and ensure product information is correctly structured and controlled within the PLM environment.
• Analyse engineering and PLM data to identify configuration gaps, inconsistencies and data-quality issues.
• Ensure consistency between PLM, ERP, engineering drawings, specifications and BOM structures.
• Coordinate configuration change control processes and support Change Control Boards (CCBs).
• Ensure engineering changes are documented, assessed, approved, implemented and fully traceable.
• Maintain accurate configuration status records and documentation throughout the product lifecycle.
• Participate in engineering and design reviews, including PDR and CDR.
• Support configuration audits and ensure compliance with relevant standards and processes.
• Establish, maintain and release configuration documentation at key project milestones.
• Work closely with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Project Management teams.
• Identify opportunities to improve Configuration Management processes, tools and governance.
• Support continuous improvement of configuration data integrity and product information management within the PLM environment.

Qualifications
Requirements:
• Minimum 5 years' experience in Configuration Management within an engineering, technical or data management environment.
• Strong knowledge of Configuration Management principles, processes and best practices.
• Working knowledge of ISO 10007.
• Strong understanding of configuration planning, identification, control, status accounting and configuration audits.
• Strong understanding of technical documentation, product structures, BOMs, Configuration Items and configuration baselines.
• Experience with engineering change management, change control and configuration traceability.
• Experience with PLM/PDM systems, ideally Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or similar.
• Ability to analyse engineering/product data and identify inconsistencies or configuration issues.
• Good understanding of the relationship between PLM, ERP, drawings, specifications and BOM/product structures.
• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
• Ability to work autonomously within a multidisciplinary engineering environment.
• CMII certification or equivalent practical Configuration Management experience would be advantageous.
• Relevant higher education qualification or equivalent professional experience.
Desirable:
• Experience within Aerospace, Space, Defence/Military, Automotive or other highly regulated engineering environments.
• Experience with Windchill, particularly configuration management, product structures, BOMs, data quality or PLM migration.
• Experience working with sensitive or controlled data.
• Experience supporting or leading Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), configuration audits and engineering change processes.
• Experience with PDR/CDR and formal engineering development environments.
• French or German language skills.
Senior / Lead Configuration Manager:
For the Senior/Lead position, we are looking for significant Configuration Management experience.
The successful candidate should be able to operate autonomously, guide other Configuration Managers and improve Configuration Management governance, processes and data integrity.
The Senior/Lead profile should be comfortable resolving complex configuration and product-data issues, supporting CCBs and audits, and working across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain and Project teams.

Additional Information
Working Environment:
The role is based in Pitstone.
Due to the recent PLM migration, the initial period will require a strong onsite presence for onboarding, knowledge transfer and collaboration with the existing team.
Initial working pattern: 3–4 days onsite per week.
Once established, there may be scope to reduce onsite attendance to approximately 1 day per week, depending on experience, project requirements and team needs.
Contract: Initial 6-month requirement, with expected extension.

About This Job
For Universal ​United Kingdom Resort ​(UUKR), This position provides leadership to a multi-disciplinary team responsible for the planning, design, construction, and commissioning of infrastructure and property development projects and associated resort complex (ERC). The Project Director oversees all aspects of enabling public roadways, bridges, and construction logistics across the ERC, ensuring successful project delivery aligned with budget, schedule, quality, safety, creative, and guest experience objectives.
Responsibilities include directing project strategy, planning, commercial management, stakeholder coordination, design integration, construction execution, and commissioning activities. The role also focuses on minimising project risks, claims, disputes, change orders, and interface disruptions while maintaining strong control of schedule, budget, quality, and field operations. Success in this role requires hands-on leadership, effective collaboration across project participants, and the development of high-performing internal, consultant, and contractor teams supported by efficient document control processes.
• Work with Universal Destinations & Experiences (UDX) leadership and provide direction to multi-departmental project teams including Universal Creative, Finance, Operations, Procurement, Legal, External Affairs, Security, EHS, etc. to establish scope and schedule requirements, develop budgets and financial planning, manage procurement, address SDO conditions and governmental commitments, and complete design, construction and commissioning.
• Oversee overall project safety, obtain final acceptance for a contractor’s submitted safety plan, and compliance with Environment Health & Safety (EHS) standards.
• Manage the planning and execution of enabling infrastructure and developments such as public roadways and bridges. Manage and responsible for the overarching site logistics across ERC, in accordance with CDM and statutory and SDO requirements. Manage the planning and integration of construction works pertaining to third party development across the ERC, including rail station and supporting developments.
• Ensure that all project procedures are being followed as it relates to correspondence, RFI’s, directives, design and construction drawings, submittals, meeting minutes, action trackers, default lists, notices, pay applications, etc. necessary to successfully complete works to enable theme park and resort construction.
• Responsible for maintaining the overall project budget and schedule within the targeted objectives set forth during project approval.
• Provide leadership and personal development guidance to all direct reports to support growth within current positions and opportunities for additional growth and advancement within UDX.
• Responsible for the management, tracking and reporting of all the necessary project components inclusive of budget, schedule and progress of the project to upper management.
• Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established Universal policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications
• Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent qualifications in Engineering, Construction, Management or a related field is required.
• Experience of construction project management, in project management, engineering, construction or commercial facilities industry.
• Experience in the delivery of infrastructure construction projects design and construction phases.
• Experience in project scheduling, estimating, bidding process and negotiations.
• Strong knowledge of construction project delivery methods for enabling infrastructure, including roadways, rail development, and roadway structures.
• Experience working with third-party developers and managing complex stakeholder relationships.
• Experience with bespoke contracts, development agreements, and contract administration.
• Ability to interpret design and construction drawings, specifications, and technical documentation.
• Experience in scheduling, estimating, critical path management, site logistics, and constructability reviews.
• Strong understanding of construction and project management processes across all project phases.
• Experience managing project finances, including budgets, cash flow, cost control, and change orders.
• Effective leadership, communication, and coordination skills across multiple stakeholders, vendors, consultants, and contractors.
• Hands-on approach to field operations, maintaining operational continuity during construction and ensuring efficient document control.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Project, Planner, Power BI, Teams, Power Apps.
• Bluebeam or equivalent Portable Document Format (PDF) software. AutoCAD and Revit preferred.
• Role may require regular travel across the UK, with occasional international travel.
• SIA licensing and/or relevant executive security certifications preferred.

Additional Information
As part of our selection process, external candidates may be required to attend an in-person interview with an NBCUniversal employee at one of our locations prior to a hiring decision. Technical & Quality Centre
Quality Product Analysis Specialist
Location: Rotherham
Alliance Automotive Group UK & Ireland is a leading distributor of passenger and commercial vehicle parts to motor factors, garages, franchise networks and public services throughout the UK and Ireland. Our strategically designed network, supported by acquisitions, positions us as a market leader in providing automotive parts distribution services to the aftermarket.
Supported by a top-tier logistics network comprising over 300 local stores, 20 Regional Distribution Centres, our state-of-the-art 1 million square foot National Distribution Centre, and a workforce of over 6,000 colleagues, our business model prioritises maintaining an extensive and readily available product range to uphold the quality of our service offerings.
The Quality Product Analysis Specialist plays a critical role within the Technical & Quality Centre by conducting in-depth inspections, diagnostic testing, and root cause analysis of returned automotive components.
This position ensures that warranty claims are assessed accurately and consistently while supporting overall product quality, compliance, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Working across a broad range of systems—including turbochargers, braking components, suspension units, clutches, and rotating electrics (alternators and starters)—the specialist applies advanced mechanical and electrical expertise to determine failure causes, verify product performance against factory specifications, and differentiate between manufacturing defects and usage-related issues.
The role combines hands-on technical evaluation with detailed digital reporting and cross-functional collaboration. Using specialized testing equipment and precision measuring tools, the specialist generates comprehensive inspection reports, documents findings with photographic evidence, and supports warranty decision-making in alignment with company policies and regulatory standards.
Beyond technical capability, the position requires strong analytical thinking and a methodical, investigative mindset. The Quality Product Analysis Specialist acts as a key liaison between warranty administration, customer service, and manufacturing partners—clearly communicating technical findings to ensure timely and fair claim resolution.
This role is essential in safeguarding product integrity, improving quality performance, and maintaining customer confidence through accurate, data-driven analysis and professional technical expertise.
Core Responsibilities
• Component Inspection: Conduct detailed physical and functional inspections on a wide range of components including turbos, braking systems, suspension units, clutches, and rotating electrics (alternators/starters).
• Diagnostic Testing: Operate specialised test equipment (e.g., vacuum testers, electronic actuator testers, battery/alternator analysers, brake DTV machines, and brake caliper testers) to verify part performance against factory specifications.
• Root Cause Analysis: Investigate and determine the underlying cause of failure (e.g., carbon buildup, oil starvation, electrical surges, installation errors) to support warranty claim evaluations.
• Warranty Claim Assessment: Review and assess warranty claims in accordance with company policies, determining validity and identifying potential manufacturing or usage defects.
• Digital Reporting & Documentation: Utilise computer systems to log findings, upload digital photos of defects, generate professional inspection and warranty evaluation reports, and maintain accurate records for claim processing.
• Quality & Compliance: Maintain a clean, organised laboratory/testing environment ensuring all test equipment is in safe and calibrated working order. Ensure inspections comply with company standards and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Cross-Functional Communication: Collaborate closely with warranty administration, customer service, and re manufacturing teams to share findings, explain technical details, and support timely claim resolution.
Technical Skills & Knowledge (Hard Skills)
• Multi-System Mastery: Deep mechanical knowledge of modern vehicle and electronic systems.
• Electrical Proficiency: Ability to read electrical schematics and use multimetres or oscilloscopes to test rotating electrics and electronic sensors.
• Software Literacy: Comfortable with PC-based diagnostic software, CRM portals, warranty management systems, and standard office tools (e.g., Microsoft Word/Excel).
• Precision Measurement: Skilled with precision tools such as micrometres, vernier calipers, and dial indicators for checking tolerances and shaft play.
• Warranty & Compliance Knowledge: Understanding of warranty policies, claim processing procedures, and applicable regulatory standards.
Character Qualities & Professionalism (Soft Skills)
• Analytical Thinking: Logical, detective-like mindset adept at solving complex diagnostic puzzles that other technicians may overlook.
• Attention to Detail: Precision in inspecting fracture surfaces, wear patterns, and minute electrical deviations.
• Reliability & Punctuality: Strict adherence to schedules and deadlines, ensuring customer and warranty reports are delivered on time.
• Clear Communication: Ability to translate complex technical failures into clear, simple language for non-technical stakeholders, customers, and internal teams.
• Collaboration: Effective team player with proven ability to coordinate across departments for efficient warranty handling.
Desired Qualifications & Experience
• Proven Experience: Ideally 3–5 years as a senior technician or diagnostic specialist in a high-volume garage, remanufacturing environment, or warranty inspection role.
• Certification: Level 3 Automotive Technician qualification or equivalent (e.g., IMI or City & Guilds).
• Failure Analysis Training. Warranty Training: Experience or formal training related to warranty claim evaluation and processing preferred.
Physical Requirements
• Capacity to safely handle heavy components (e.g., alternators, brake discs) and stand for extended periods in a workshop or laboratory environment.
