CS3 operates across the UK, developing and delivering innovative support solutions and services that help our customers keep critical capabilities available wherever and whenever they are needed.
Our nine-week Summer Placement is designed to give you meaningful experience within a relatively short period. You will typically work on a defined project or investigation focused on a real CS3 engineering challenge, giving you the opportunity to explore a problem, work with engineers and stakeholders, develop and evaluate ideas, and communicate your findings and recommendations. Projects are likely to support the development of CS3's engineering capability and could involve areas such as new technologies, data and information, engineering methods and tools, or new approaches to how we design and deliver support solutions. You will work as part of a team throughout your placement, whether undertaking a defined investigation or contributing to a broader range of ongoing engineering activities.
You won't be expected to know everything when you join. Throughout your placement, you'll work alongside experienced engineers and subject matter experts who will help you understand the context behind your project and provide technical guidance. You'll also receive coaching and support from your team and our dedicated CS3 Early Careers Manager. You will also have opportunities to engage with other early careers colleagues and the wider engineering community, helping you gain an understanding of the different career opportunities available within Leonardo.
As your understanding and confidence grow, you'll have the opportunity to take ownership of elements of your project, explore ideas and apply what you've learned at university in a practical engineering environment. There will also be opportunities to get involved in STEM activities with local schools.
Our aim is for a Summer Placement to be the start of your journey with us. Successful placements may lead to opportunities to return for future placements or, where appropriate, join our Graduate Programme after completing your studies.
This is a nine-week placement based at our Luton site. Leonardo also operates a Custom (hybrid) working model that allows employees to split their time between attending the workplace and working remotely, subject to the needs of the placement, project and team.
What you'll do as a Summer Placement Systems Engineering (Customer Support):
Your exact activities will depend on your placement project or the team you join, but you could:
• Apply and develop your technical knowledge to investigate a real engineering problem or opportunity.
• Understand the problem and its wider context, including the needs of relevant customers and stakeholders.
• Gather, analyse and interpret information or data to develop your understanding and support engineering decisions.
• Explore potential solutions, approaches or improvements, considering their benefits, limitations and wider implications.
• Use Systems Engineering techniques such as requirements analysis, modelling, option assessment or structured problem solving, where appropriate to your project.
• Work collaboratively with engineers and specialists from different disciplines, learning from their expertise and contributing your own ideas and perspectives.
• Develop practical experience of how engineering activities are undertaken within an organisation, including the processes, methods and tools used to deliver high-quality technical work.
• Document and communicate your work clearly, sharing your findings, conclusions or recommendations with relevant stakeholders.
• Contribute to engineering capability and process improvement, where relevant to your placement.
• Contribute to the design, development, integration, verification or support of complex systems and support solutions.
The exact activities will vary depending on the team and area you join, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad understanding of Systems Engineering while building your technical knowledge and practical experience.
What we need from you:
You will need:
• To be currently studying an undergraduate or postgraduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or another STEM subject.
• An interest in engineering and enthusiasm for developing your understanding of Systems Engineering in an industry environment.
We are also looking for people who can demonstrate some of the following through their studies, university projects, work experience, extracurricular activities or other experiences:
• Curiosity and a logical approach to solving unfamiliar problems.
• Self-motivation and a proactive approach to learning and problem solving.
• The ability to consider both the detail of a problem and the wider system or context.
• A willingness to investigate a topic, ask questions and use evidence to develop your understanding.
• A collaborative approach and willingness to learn from, and share ideas with, people from different technical and professional backgrounds.
• The ability to organise and prioritise your work and take ownership of tasks, seeking guidance where appropriate.
• Confidence to ask questions, constructively challenge ideas and speak up when something doesn't look right.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information and ideas to different audiences.
• A willingness to seek feedback, learn from experience and try new approaches.
You do not need previous experience of the defence or aerospace industry. We are interested in your potential, your approach to problem solving and your willingness to learn. This is not an exhaustive list, and we encourage you to apply even if you don't yet have experience in all of the areas above. We recognise that a Summer Placement is an opportunity to develop your skills and experience. A positive attitude, curiosity and a willingness to learn are some of the most important qualities we're looking for.

accenture.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/accent.description_excerpt:
Management Consultant - Communications & Media
Career Level 9: Consultant
Location: London
As a team
We work with leading organisations in telecoms, TV and broadcast, gaming and betting, sport, business media and publishing. Their networks, services and content reach millions of people and businesses every day, and almost everything about how they operate is being rethought.
Audiences now move freely between screens, services and devices. Customers expect digital experiences that simply work. AI is changing how products are built, how content is made and how businesses run. For the organisations we serve, this is a moment to reinvent rather than tweak.
We help them work out what to build, and then we help them build it. Our work spans network and telecoms reinvention, customer experience, the way content is produced, managed and monetised, and the creation of new digital products and services.
As a Consultant, you will sit where consulting meets product delivery. You will help clients get clear on the problem and their ambition, and then stay involved as that thinking becomes a product, platform or service that real customers use. You don't need to be an engineer, but you will enjoy working alongside engineers, designers and data specialists. You will get into the detail and make the practical trade-offs that turn a good idea into something that ships.
Challenges you could work on
• Simplifying a telecoms operator's products and the systems behind them, so new services launch in weeks rather than years.
• Redesigning how consumers and businesses buy, set up and get help with their broadband, mobile and connectivity services.
• Modernising the platforms that bring programmes and live sport to audiences across apps, TVs and devices.
• Using AI to speed up how content is tagged, edited, localised and discovered.
• Creating new products, commercial models and revenue streams from content, audiences, advertising and intellectual property.
• Helping a betting or gaming operator improve how its products are designed, built and released.
• Changing the people, processes, technology and data behind a core part of a client's business, rather than simply replacing its systems.
In our team you will learn
• How Communications and Media businesses really work, from network to content to customer, by working with leading organisations in the sector.
• How to take an idea from discovery through to launch, drawing on Accenture's engineering, design, data and AI specialists.
• How to apply AI and data to real problems, and how to tell a promising use case from a distraction.
In this role you will
• Help clients turn business problems and customer needs into clear product visions, roadmaps and plans that teams can deliver.
• Take responsibility for a defined product area or workstream, helping to move it from discovery and design through build, launch and improvement.
• Work day to day with client and Accenture teams across product, engineering, design and data, helping them prioritise, resolve delivery challenges and make practical trade-offs.
• Build business cases and success measures that link what gets built to the outcomes it should deliver, and use data to show whether it is working.
• Find practical ways to use AI in products, customer experiences and operations.
• Run interviews and workshops, present to clients, and help business and technology teams reach a shared view.
• Contribute to proposals and new opportunities, and play an active part in the life of the team.
Job qualifications
We are looking for people who enjoy both shaping ideas and making them happen. You will be able to point to products, services or business capabilities that you have helped design, build, launch or transform.
With around four years' relevant experience, you may have built your career in consulting, a Communications or Media business, a digital agency, a product studio or a technology company. Your experience might include consulting, business analysis, product ownership or product management. We welcome different paths, and we don't expect you to bring everything below.
Product and delivery
• You have helped design and deliver digital products, platforms or services, and contributed to a roadmap, backlog or workstream along the way.
• You can turn strategy into clear priorities and requirements, and make sensible trade-offs between customer value, cost, speed and technical feasibility.
• You can point to outcomes you helped deliver for customers, operations or revenue.
Technology and data
• You understand how digital products are built and run, and can work confidently with engineering and technology leaders.
• You know what AI, cloud and modern data platforms make possible, and can spot where they would add real value.
• You use data to inform decisions, and can build a business case that stands up to senior scrutiny.
Industry knowledge
• You have experience in, or a strong and growing understanding of, telecoms, media or both. Depth in one area, such as networks, broadcast, betting or publishing, matters more than breadth across all of them.
• You have a point of view on how changing customer expectations, AI and new commercial models are reshaping these industries.

bristolmyerssquibb.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com.description_excerpt:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Your work will reach patients. Let's talk about how.
Every medicine that makes it to a patient starts as a complex chemistry problem. Someone has to take a process that works seamlessly in a lab flask and make it work safely, reliably and at scale - in a manufacturing facility.
That someone could be you.
At Bristol Myers Squibb, we're looking for a Process Engineer to join our Chemical Process Development (CPD) team in Moreton, UK. CPD delivers clinical supplies and process development for all synthetic and anti-body drug conjugate (ADC) drug substances at BMS. This is a role where your engineering depth and your interpersonal skills will directly shape how - and how quickly - our clinical work reaches the patients who need them.
So, what does the role actually look like day-to-day?
You'll sit at the dynamic intersection between our internal science teams and the external Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations (CDMOs) who bring our processes to life at scale.
On any given week, you might be:
• Reviewing a batch record for a hazardous chemistry campaign, making sure everything from safety and quality controls to process intent is technically accurate and operationally feasible  before it goes near a plant
• Walking a CDMO facility, either virtually or in person, assessing whether their equipment and capabilities are the right fit and if not, articulating exactly why and what needs to change
• Troubleshooting a manufacturing issue, drawing on your engineering fundamentals and collaboration skillset to find the root cause and get things back on track
• Presenting risk assessments and recommendations to leadership, translating complex technical realities into clear, actionable decisions
• Building strong relationships with CDMO partners across the world – to improve how we work together and so that when things get difficult (and sometimes they will), you already have the trust in the room
What's in it for you?
Let's be direct about the real value this role offers you as a professional:
• You'll work across the full range of chemical engineering unit operations — reaction, crystallisation, distillation, extraction, filtration, drying, and milling — applied to pharmaceutical small molecule/ADC scale-up.
• Real influence across teams and organisations This role demands - and rewards - the ability to drive technical negotiations, influence cross-functional teams, and build trusted working relationships with external partners. For the right person, this is where your interpersonal skills become as professionally valuable as your engineering ones.
• A global role with a local base You'll be based at our Moreton, UK site but working closely with colleagues across the Atlantic - including your direct line manager in the US – and with CDMOs around the world. With up to 50% remote working available, you get flexibility without losing the connection and collaboration that makes this kind of work rewarding.
• Variety beyond the desk Up to 20% international travel means you'll be on-site at CDMOs and in facilities.
• A platform to grow and give back BMS actively values mentorship and knowledge-sharing. Whether it's developing colleagues, contributing to communities of practice, or helping shape how the function works - this is a role where building others up is part of the job, not an afterthought.
Is this you?
• You'll bring a B.Eng. or M.Eng. in Chemical Engineering and at least 10–15 years of industrial manufacturing experience - ideally in pharmaceutical drug substance manufacturing and GMP environments. Experience in specialty chemical or petrochemical industries is also acceptable.
• You know how to read a lab protocol and visualise how it will operate in a manufacturing environment.
• You can spot scale-up risk before it becomes a manufacturing incident.
• You have a strong grounding in chemical engineering fundamentals across reaction, crystallisation, distillation, extraction, filtration, drying, and milling
• But just as importantly: you communicate clearly, you adapt your approach to the audience and the stakes, and you're comfortable managing complexity across multiple workstreams and stakeholders at once.
• Experience in lab-based small molecule development? Useful, but not essential.
Please note: This position requires work within facilities handling hazardous chemical agents, which, if improperly handled, may have the potential to affect employee health, including reproductive function and/or embryo/fetal development.
Why BMS, why now?
BMS is a company that has approved treatments that have genuinely changed what's possible in oncology, immunology, cardiovascular disease, and beyond. Our pipeline continues to grow — and the work of our Chemical Process Development team is central to keeping it moving.
When you get this right, patients get their medicine sooner. That's the job.
Ready to apply? We'd love to hear from you.

The London Stock Exchange Group seeks an experienced, dedicated and driven Attack Monitoring Analyst to join the Global Security Operations team!
ROLE SUMMARY:
LSEG Security Operations is a central function employing people, process and technology to continuously monitor and respond to cyber security incidents.
This role is for an Attack Monitoring Analyst for the Global Security Operations Centre (GSOC). The role is responsible for identifying and responding to cyber security incidents and improving the defensive capabilities of the GSOC.
The ideal candidate will have a solid technical background, with a firm understanding of modern attack techniques coupled with knowledge of the typical lifecycle of an attack.
SHIFT:
Role operates on a "follow-the-sun" shift rotation. Shifts are 1200hrs - 0000hrs (midday to midnight) London Time using a 4 days on, 4 days off rotation.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Triage security events and employ a methodical and coherent response to security incidents adopting playbooks where necessary.
• Competently operate a chosen SIEM (e.g. Splunk/QRadar/LogRhythm) for incident investigations, or for the development of monitoring dashboards.
• Utilise playbooks, existing knowledge and accurate online resources for guidance when responding to incidents.
• Utilise online resources for researching and collecting threat intelligence to improve the SOC’s abilities to detect cyber-attacks.
• Develop new, or improve existing run books and use cases based on investigations and knowledge of modern attacks.
• Stay up to date with current vulnerabilities, attacks, and countermeasures.
• Identify, respond and remediate cyber events generated through monitoring technologies.
EXPERIENCE:
• Preferred experience with operating or administrating a SIEM (e.g. Splunk/QRadar/LogRhythm).
• Solid understanding of networks including the TCP/IP stack, typical organisation architectures, and common protocols abused by malware.
• Experience in security event analysis & triage, incident handling and root-cause identification.
• Understanding of tools, techniques and procedures that attackers use to compromise organisations, ideally from direct experience.
• Knowledge of cyber security either academically or within corporate environments.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced and demanding environment while remaining calm.
• Strong verbal and written communication and collaboration skills.
• Security industry specific and core technical accreditations such as OSCP, GIAC, CCNA.
• Certification demonstrating SIEM operational competences.
• Proficient with one or more programming languages (e.g. Python, PowerShell, Java, C#).

As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.
About the Role
The Threat Analyst joins the Emerging Threats and Security Validation team within the CrowdStrike Malware Research Center (MRC). This team plays a critical role in understanding today's threat landscape, identifying gaps in Falcon's detection capabilities, and helping improve CrowdStrike's protection through threat research, automation, AI, and machine learning.
Working closely with Threat Research, Engineering, Data Science, and Red Team teams, you'll investigate emerging threats, validate detection coverage, and translate technical research into product improvements that better protect our customers. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex technical problems while making a direct impact on our products.
What You'll Do:
•
Research and analyse emerging malware and cyber threats to understand how they impact our customers.
•
Investigate malware across the full attack lifecycle (adversary kill chain) to ensure Falcon detects and stops threats at every stage.
•
Distinguish genuine threats from background noise by analysing data from multiple internal and external sources.
•
Validate and improve CrowdStrike's detection capabilities by identifying gaps and working with engineering teams to strengthen our protections.
•
Support external security testing and certification programmes (such as AV-Test, AV-Comparatives, and SE Labs) by analysing test results and helping address any missed detections.
•
Respond to newly discovered threats by performing technical investigations and recommending the best approach for detection and prevention.
•
Partner with Threat Research, Engineering, Red Team, and Machine Learning teams to translate research into product improvements.
•
Help design and improve automation that reduces manual effort and accelerates threat analysis.
•
Communicate technical findings clearly to engineering and response teams to enable faster and more effective action.
•
Contribute to the continuous evolution of Falcon by combining malware research, automation, AI, and machine learning to improve customer protection.
What You'll Need:
•
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
•
4+ years of experience in threat research with a focus on malware analysis.
•
Experience reverse engineering file-based malware, exploits, and other attack techniques. Industry certifications such as GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM) are desirable.
•
Strong understanding of disassembly and structured programming principles.
•
Deep knowledge of at least one major operating system and its internals to support behaviour-based analysis.
•
Strong understanding of the adversary kill chain and attacker behaviour, with experience applying red team methodologies to validate defensive coverage. Certifications such as Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP) are desirable.
•
Experience collaborating with engineering teams to turn research into production capabilities.
•
Ability to develop small automation or scripting projects to solve immediate technical challenges.
•
Experience contributing to public security testing programmes (such as AV-Test, AV-Comparatives, or SE Labs) is a plus.
•
Experience working with large datasets and tools such as Splunk, Elasticsearch, or Kibana is a plus.
•
Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.
About the Malware Research Center:
The CrowdStrike Malware Research Center is the core of Falcon’s malware detection and response capabilities. The team has a focus on understanding the threat landscape and sets the target for what Falcon should be identifying and preventing. Additionally, the MRC is responsible for understanding our capabilities, and mapping how well our machine learning and behavioral protection capabilities are doing against those threats. Where there is a gap, the MRC takes action to improve our detection stance, and improve our overall protection story. MRC also performs pathfinding research to enable technology development using innovation, prototyping and bleeding edge machine learning to support our flagship Falcon product. There are many parts of CrowdStrike working towards protecting customer environments, and the MRC works across all of them to ensure we are on target and providing the best protection for our current Threat landscape.
Emerging Threats and Security Validation Team:
Leading the charge for understanding the activity of malware today is the Emerging Threats and Security Validation team. With a focus on malware research, the primary role of the team is to understand the threats and malware that are affecting our customer’s businesses. The challenge is the enormous scale of malware today and the sheer number of samples required to be addressed, which requires a more creative approach than traditional Anti-Virus research. Using the data amassed from CrowdStrike’s capabilities and products, we take a holistic view of the threat landscape and identify the emerging threats that are likely to affect our business in the short to medium term. Human efforts are bolstered by automation, AI enrichment, and machine learning to protect our customers when they need it most.

Make your mark at one of the biggest names in payments. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer – Agentic Commerce to join our ever-evolving agentic commerce engineering team and help shape the future of global commerce.

We are building the future of autonomous commerce. AI Agent Integrations
•
Design and build secure checkout and payment APIs that AI agents can invoke reliably and deterministically, including support for concepts such as UCP, ACP, AP2, agentic tokens, delegated credentials, verifiable intent, and MPP.
•
Implement flows that capture and validate agent context, user intent, delegated authority, payment credentials, risk signals, transaction evidence, and downstream reporting data.
•
Integrate agentic commerce capabilities with global payment platforms, gateways, checkout, tokenization, authentication, fraud, reporting, and merchant-facing systems.
API & SDK Development
•
Build merchant-facing APIs, SDKs, documentation, sample flows, sandbox experiences, and developer tools that make agentic commerce easier to adopt.
•
Design for clear contracts, predictable errors, strong validation, fast testing, and measurable time-to-first-transaction.
•
Use feedback from internal teams, external developers, pilots, and partner integrations to improve the platform quickly.
Backend Engineering
•
Build Java-based backend services that support real-time, high-trust payment workflows with strong performance, observability, security, and operational discipline.

Own features from design through implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
•
Contribute to design reviews, code reviews, service documentation, production readiness, and a culture of high-quality engineering.
What you’ll bring
•
5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and operating production services, APIs, distributed systems, or transaction-processing applications.
•
Experience building and operating cloud-based systems on AWS, Google Cloud Platform, or comparable public cloud environments, with strong fundamentals in deployment, monitoring, reliability, and secure service design.
•
Practical interest in AI agents and agentic workflows, including how agents call APIs, pass structured data, operate within delegated permissions, and require validation before triggering real-world actions.
•
Strong software engineering fundamentals across API design, testing, CI/CD, observability, secure coding, resilience, maintainability, and production support.
•
Ability to collaborate across product, architecture, security, fraud, checkout, tokenization, gateway, and platform teams to deliver cross-system capabilities in a fast-moving, emerging product area.

Experience in payments, fintech, commerce, gateways, card-not-present processing, checkout, tokenization, 3DS/SCA, fraud/risk, disputes, merchant reporting, or other high-trust transaction systems.

Experience building or integrating with AI-powered applications, agent frameworks, LLM tool-calling patterns, MCP-style integrations, A2A-style workflows, structured automation systems, or safe AI execution patterns such as validation, policy checks, audit logs, fallback paths, and protection against prompt injection or tool misuse.
•
Hands-on experience with Node.js, TypeScript, SDKs, developer tooling, sandbox environments, sample apps, merchant-facing APIs, GitHub projects, open-source tools, standards discussions, AI engineering communities, or technical forums.

Do you have experience of supporting individuals with physical health, mental health, social or practical barriers to remain in work, return to work or secure new employment?
Then consider the role of Neighbourhood Work & Health Coach at Reed in Partnership!

What is the role about?
WorkWell is an integrated work and health support service helping people with disabilities and health conditions to start, stay and succeed in work. The service provides early intervention support to individuals whose health is affecting their ability to work, helping them to overcome barriers, improve wellbeing and achieve sustainable employment outcomes.
The Neighbourhood Work & Health Coach will provide personalised, person-centred support to individuals experiencing physical health, mental health or wider wellbeing challenges that impact on their employment. Working closely with healthcare professionals, employers, community organisations and other support services, the postholder will help participants remain in work, return to work following absence, or move into suitable employment.
Through coaching, assessment and coordinated case management, the Neighbourhood Work & Health Coach will support participants to develop practical solutions to health and employment barriers. They will work as part of a multi-disciplinary team (MDT), helping participants access specialist interventions, community support and workplace adjustments that enable sustainable employment and improved wellbeing.
Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
• Conduct comprehensive biopsychosocial assessments to understand the relationship between a participant's health, wellbeing and employment circumstances.
• Build trusted and supportive relationships with participants through a person-centred coaching approach.
• Use motivational interviewing and behaviour change techniques to identify strengths, aspirations, barriers and opportunities.
• Develop personalised Work and Health Action Plans that include employment, wellbeing and personal goals.
• Identify physical health, mental health, social and practical barriers affecting a participant's ability to remain in work, return to work or secure new employment.
• Provide ongoing coaching, guidance and practical support to help participants improve confidence, wellbeing and work readiness.
• Support participants to remain in employment through early intervention, workplace problem-solving and appropriate workplace adjustment planning.
• Work with participants who are absent from work to develop structured return-to-work plans, including phased returns where appropriate.
• Coordinate interventions and referrals that address identified barriers, ensuring support is timely, proportionate and outcome-focused.
• Provide employment coaching including career planning, job search support, CV development and interview preparation where appropriate.
• Work closely with clinicians, social prescribers, health coaches, occupational health professionals and community support providers to coordinate integrated support plans.
• Identify, assess and appropriately escalate safeguarding, welfare and risk concerns in accordance with organisational policies and procedures.
What’s in it for you?
A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:
• 25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays
• Reed Pension Scheme
• Award Winning Management & Leadership training
• Professional & Personal Development Funds
• Bi-annual pay reviews
• Plus much more that can be found on our website
• With the chance to dramatically make a difference to the local community, this role offers immense job satisfaction.
At Reed in Partnership, we live and breathe our values in every decision and action taken, resulting in a collaborative and enjoyable culture within our offices. Our company values – we are fair open and honest; we take ownership, and we work together.
To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:

• Experience managing a caseload and supporting individuals to achieve agreed outcomes.
• Experience working in partnership with multiple organisations and stakeholders.

• Experience supporting individuals to remain in work or return to work following sickness absence.

About Waythrough
Waythrough was formed in 2024 following the merger of Humankind and Richmond Fellowship. Together, we’ve created one of the largest mental health and social support charities in England.
Every year, we support around 125,000 people through nearly 200 services – and it’s all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.
Make a real difference in your community
Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.
About the role
At Waythrough, we’re looking for a compassionate and motivated Social Isolation Support Coordinator to join our Community Services team. This is an exciting opportunity to join a new role supporting adults aged 55 and over who may be experiencing loneliness, social isolation, poor mental wellbeing or difficulties accessing their local community.
You’ll work directly with individuals on a one-to-one basis, helping them build confidence, improve their wellbeing and develop meaningful social connections. You’ll support people to identify their goals, explore opportunities within their communities and access the services and activities that can make a real difference to their lives.
As this is a new role, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how the service develops, build relationships with local organisations and demonstrate the positive impact this support can have. Your work will help us show commissioners the value of the service and its potential to improve outcomes for local people.
What will you be doing?
As a Social Isolation Support Coordinator, you will:
• Work with individuals to understand their needs, strengths, goals and the barriers they face.
• Develop personalised support plans focused on improving wellbeing, confidence and independence.
• Provide practical and emotional support to people experiencing loneliness, anxiety, low confidence or social isolation.
• Help individuals access local community groups, activities, volunteering opportunities and other support services.
• Accompany people to initial appointments or community activities where appropriate, helping them feel confident taking the next steps.
• Provide information, advice and signposting to relevant health, social care, housing, welfare and community services.
• Build positive working relationships with local organisations and community partners.
• Monitor progress, review support plans and maintain accurate records of outcomes.
• Recognise safeguarding concerns and follow the appropriate procedures to help keep people safe.
You’ll work independently, managing your own caseload while building a strong network of local connections to help people access the support they need.
What are we looking for?
We’re looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic and confident in building relationships with people from a range of backgrounds. You’ll understand the impact loneliness and social isolation can have on someone’s life and be passionate about helping people feel valued, connected and empowered.
You will have:
• Experience working with vulnerable adults, older people or individuals with wellbeing needs.
• An understanding of the causes and impact of loneliness and social isolation.
• Experience assessing individual needs and developing support plans.
• Knowledge of safeguarding principles and procedures.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
• The ability to motivate and empower individuals to achieve positive outcomes.
• The ability to work independently and manage your own caseload.
• A full driving licence and access to a vehicle, as required for the role.
A relevant qualification in health and social care, community development, counselling, advice and guidance, or a related field would be desirable.
Experience in social prescribing, community navigation or wellbeing support would also be beneficial. However, we welcome applications from people with transferable skills who can demonstrate the ability to engage effectively with individuals and build positive, trusting relationships.

What We Offer
We value the people who make a difference every day. Alongside meaningful work, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package:

27 days’ annual leave, rising to 32 after 1 year (plus bank holidays)
•
Pension scheme with 4.5% employer contribution, matched up to 6.5%

Life assurance (3× annual salary)

Birthday leave and the option to buy up to 5 extra days’ annual leave

Professional fee reimbursement for relevant qualifications

24/7 online GP access and Employee Assistance Programme

Recognition and long service awards via our Way to Go and Aspirations portals
•
£500 Recommend a Friend bonus
•
Cycle to Work scheme and Credit Union membership
•
Discounts via Blue Light Card, Charity Discounts, Extras and Tickets for Good
•
Free will writing service and wellbeing initiatives throughout the year

Join us at Entrust
At Entrust, we’re shaping the future of identity centric security solutions. From our comprehensive portfolio of solutions to our flexible, global workplace, we empower careers, foster collaboration, and build solutions that help keep the world moving safely.
Get to Know Us
Headquartered in Minnesota, Entrust is an industry leader in identity-centric security solutions, serving over 150 countries with cutting-edge, scalable technologies. But our secret weapon? Our people. It’s the curiosity, dedication, and innovation that drive our success and help us anticipate the future.
We are looking for an experienced Policy and Regulatory Analyst to join our Product Regulatory Compliance team.
About the role:
Europe is rewriting the rules of digital identity. eIDAS 2.0 and the EUDI Wallet, the AI Act, EU AML regulation, the certification frameworks beneath them: everything is changing at once. All of this at a moment when fighting fraud - deepfakes and other AI-powered attacks - has never mattered more.
Entrust builds technology at the centre of it all: AI-powered identity verification and biometrics, and the connections to the EUDI Wallet and new eID schemes that are becoming Europe’s identity infrastructure. Our Public & Regulatory Affairs team sits inside the Product organisation to make sure we don't just follow the new rules - we contribute to shaping them.
This is a role for the curious: you’ll be the expert colleagues consult, the first to read the texts that will reshape the sector, and the guiding voice of policy in the room where the product takes shape.
What makes it a rare opportunity is where the team lives: inside Product. Your analysis feeds directly into the roadmap, and the scope runs from AI to age verification, from cyber to digital sovereignty. And because new rules open new markets as often as they impose new constraints, part of the role is spotting the opportunities they create - and bringing them to the product teams.
Reporting to the Head of Policy and Regulatory, you'll find the role is a mix:
•
A little bit of regulatory analysis...Analysing regulations (i.e. eIDAS 2.0 implementing acts, ETSI standards and EU AML regulation) as they land, and assessing what they change for our products and customers across EMEA.
•
A little bit of certification craft...Supporting our ETSI TS 119 461 v2 uplift across the EU 27 Member states, and the maintenance of our UK DVS certification - learning from the inside how Entrust gets, and stays, certified.
•
A little bit of policy and external engagement... Drafting consultation responses and position papers, joining expert working groups and industry gatherings alongside supervisors and regulators - from national authorities like ANSSI and OfDIA to the EU institutions - and travelling in Europe to meet and convince the people who write the rules.
You will also:
•
Conduct regulatory assessments across EMEA markets, covering identity, trust services and financial frameworks.
•
Help map the regulatory pathway for the EUDI Wallet.
•
Help build our horizon-scanning tooling, so we spot what's coming early.
•
Produce summaries, comparison tables and recommendations that Product, Engineering, Sales and GTM teams actually use.
Ultimately, this role is about more than tracking regulation. To be successful, you'll go deep enough to become a genuine expert, and be an important voice internally - someone who informs colleagues across teams and translates complex requirements into clear, actionable guidance. And over time, an advocate for these topics inside the company, and a voice of Entrust in the debate outside.
This role is hybrid, based in Paris or London.
What you can expect:
•
Your analysis guiding product roadmaps and strategy.
•
A growing external presence: conferences, expert working groups, and meetings with regulators and policy-makers across Europe.
•
Real ownership from day one, with the support of a senior team.
•
A nice team on top!
Essential qualifications:
•
1 to 3 years of experience in regulatory analysis, public affairs, digital identity, tech regulation or a related field.
•
Strong ability to interpret and summarise regulatory and technical frameworks (eIDAS 2.0, ETSI TS 119 461, EU AML regulation, EBA and AMLA guidelines).
•
Excellent writing, structuring and communication skills.
•
An ability to translate between the specialist languages of Product, technology and law.
•
Comfort presenting and working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales and GTM teams.
•
Fluency in English.
•
Intellectual curiosity - about the law, and about the technology behind it (deepfakes, biometrics, digital identity wallets).
Preferred qualifications:
•
Fluency in French, German or Spanish.
•
Expérience with trust services, eIDAS 2.0, ETSI standards (in particular ETSI TS 119 461) or the UK DIATF.
Exposure to certification processes (ISO, ETSI, national eKYC frameworks) or to public consultations and position papers.

We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity.
From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution — because the best ideas take time to evolve. Together we’re building a world-class platform to amplify our teams’ most powerful ideas.

Take the next step in your career.
The role
We operate an advanced systematic client trading platform. Its systems are fully automated, globally distributed and operate at extreme scale — executing millions of trades per day. Ensuring platform resilience, uptime and operational efficiency is mission-critical.
As a Software Engineer in Realtime Quant Frameworks, you’ll play a key role in helping our quant researchers move faster across our large scale compute estate — building systems that reduce the complexity of running workloads across massive compute farms and providing real-time support to keep research running smoothly and efficiently.
A key part of the role focuses on our core scheduling platform, written in F#, which distributes huge workloads across the compute farm and is accessed via Python and .NET SDKs — the main interface our quants use day-to-day.
You’ll contribute to a TypeScript/React UI, backed by an F# ASP.NET service with a Postgres database on Kubernetes, giving real-time visibility into workload progress.
Beyond that, you’ll help extend our tooling and frameworks that enable quants to build and deploy research platforms and express computations over streaming data — creating flexible, high-performance systems that go well beyond the quant finance domain.
Who are we looking for?
The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience:
• An extensive background in software engineering, ideally in distributed or high-performance systems
• Experience with F#, C#, Python or similar languages in production environments
• Experience working with Python in research or data-driven workflows
• Familiarity with modern backend and cloud-native technologies including Kubernetes and relational databases
• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work closely with quantitative researchers

• Highly competitive compensation plus annual discretionary bonus
• Lunch provided (via Just Eat for Business) and dedicated barista bar

• Comprehensive healthcare and life assurance

About SiFive
As the pioneers who introduced RISC-V to the world, SiFive is transforming the future of compute by bringing the limitless potential of RISC-V to the highest performance and most data-intensive applications in the world. SiFive’s unrivaled compute platforms are continuing to enable leading technology companies around the world to innovate, optimize and deliver the most advanced solutions of tomorrow across every market segment of chip design, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, automotive, data center, mobile, and consumer. With SiFive, the future of RISC-V has no limits.
At SiFive, we are always excited to connect with talented individuals, who are just as passionate about driving innovation and changing the world as we are.
Our constant innovation and ongoing success is down to our amazing teams of incredibly talented people, who collaborate and support each other to come up with truly groundbreaking ideas and solutions.  Solutions that will have a huge impact on people's lives; making the world a better place, one processor at a time.

To learn more about SiFive’s phenomenal success and to see why we have won the GSA’s prestigious Most Respected Private Company Award (for the fourth time!), check out our website and Glassdoor pages.
Job Description:
The Role:
SiFive is looking for hardware engineers who are passionate about designing industry-leading CPU and interconnect IP to help drive the tidal wave of adoption of RISC-V as the architecture of choice for SOC designs across a broad variety of vertical applications. We’re creating massively customizable IP and improving time-to-market by designing hardware as highly-configurable generators. We're leveraging technology and ideas from the software industry to execute hardware design with the agility of software development.
As a Power-Management/Reset/Clock Micro-Architect and RTL Design Engineer at SiFive, you will be part of a team of engineers who are passionate about designing industry-leading CPU cores and subsystems based on the revolutionary open RISC-V and TileLink architectures. You will create power management, reset, and clocking solutions that provide the central nervous system for cutting-edge RISC-V CPU and SoC IP designs. You will work in a fast-paced dynamic environment to bring new hardware IP to market quickly, with high quality and exceptional performance - delivering hardware at the speed of software!
Join us, and surf the RISC-V wave with SiFive!

•
Work with the architecture team to understand and define power management requirements.
•
Architect, design and implement core clocking, reset and power management solutions.

Microarchitecture development and specification. Ensure that knowledge is shared via clear documentation and participation in a culture of collaborative design.
•
Perform initial sandbox verification, and work with the design verification team to create and execute thorough verification test plans.
•
Work with a physical implementation team to implement and optimise physical design to meet frequency, area, power goals.
•
Work with a software team to enable and optimise power management features.

3+ years of recent industry experience in CPU and SoC clocking, reset, and power-management logic designs.
•
Experience in high-performance, energy-efficient CPU and SoC designs.

Expertise in CPU and SoC clocking, reset design, and power management, including:
•
Reset control and design strategies: Clock distribution, dynamic clocking, clock gating, and clock boundary crossing strategies
•
Power state definition and management and Power Management Unit (PMU) design
•
Dynamic and static power reduction techniques, including retention and power-up/down sequencing
•
Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and Di/dt mitigation strategies
•
Understanding of DFT, MBIST, Debug and Error handling in CPU designs
•
Power-aware simulation
•
Proficiency with hardware (RTL) design in Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VDHL.
•
Good understanding of various RTL quality checks like Lint, CDC, RDC etc. Hands-on experience with Spyglass is a plus.
•
Attention to detail and a focus on high-quality design.
•
Ability to work well with others and a belief that engineering is a team sport.
•
Knowledge of at least one object-oriented and/or functional programming language.
•
Background of successful CPU or SoC development from architecture through tapeout.
•
BS/MS degree in EE, CE, CS or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
Nice to have
•
Experience with AMBA Interconnect Protocols, such as AXI, AHB, and APB.
•
Experience with AMBA Low Power Protocol Interface, including P-channel  and Q-channel protocols.
•
Experience with Scala/Chisel, Bluespec, or some other language/DSL for expressing configurable hardware via software
•
Knowledge of RISC-V architecture
•
Experience with Git/Github, Jira, Confluence

Job Description:
We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.
About the Role:
About the role
We're building the systems that turn one of the world's largest scientific corpora into research intelligence. That means production NLP pipelines running over millions of journal articles, extracting entities, classifications, claim tuples, and summaries optimized for use by downstream agentic applications. We're looking for a senior data scientist to own domain-specific content modeling work end to end, from the eval set through the pipeline stage that ships it.
You'll join a small, senior team where data scientists own their models in production. You'll write the code, own the evaluations, ship the changes, and stay accountable for the outcomes. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to see their models through to real users in a rapidly evolving market.
What you'll do
•
Design and build NLP enrichment pipelines that extract entities, classifications, claims, and summaries from scientific full-text at scale.
•
Compare NLP approaches to extraction and enrichment against LLM-based approaches, and pick the right tool for each task. That means putting traditional NLP (NER, sequence labeling, classification), embedding-based retrieval, LLM prompting, and fine-tuned smaller models on the same table, and defending each choice with evaluation, cost, and operational tradeoffs. This is a core part of the job, not an occasional exercise.
•
Own evaluation. Build the golden sets in consultation with SMEs and vendors, choose the metrics, and make productive tradeoffs between speed, quality, and cost.
•
Write production-quality Python. Manage concurrency and cost for high-volume LLM workloads. Structure code that engineers can ship and other data scientists can extend.
•
Collaborate with a team of data engineers to orchestrate work in data pipeline and data build tools like Airflow and Dagster. Design idempotent, retryable, evaluable pipeline stages that stay reliable when a run fails at scale.
•
Contribute to agentic AI application work: tool-using systems that reason over the enriched corpus, where your NLP and evaluation background will shape how the agent grounds and defends its answers.
•
Work directly with editors, product managers, and engineers. Bring the modeling perspective into product decisions, and translate stakeholder pushback into concrete modeling work.
What you'll bring
•
Deep Python. You've written it in production, at scale, for years. You know when to reach for asyncio versus threads versus a queue, and you can explain the tradeoff clearly.
•
Strong NLP background across modern (LLMs, transformers, embeddings, retrieval) and classical (NER, classification, sequence labeling) approaches. You've built evaluations and learned from the results.
•
A habit of comparing approaches and choosing the right one for the task. You can defend "prompt a large LLM" and "train a small classifier on 2,000 labels" with equal seriousness, back the choice with an eval and a cost estimate, and know what to do when performance drifts.
•
A track record of shipping – not just prototypes and papers, but systems that deliver value to real users.
Nice to have
•
Experience working with scientific or scholarly text.
•
Familiarity with AWS (S3, Batch, Lambda, SageMaker) and Parquet or Iceberg data lake patterns.
•
Experience running LLMs under real cost and latency budgets in production.
•
Some exposure to agentic AI applications: tool use, multi-step reasoning, guardrails, and evaluation of trajectories rather than single-turn outputs.
Why us
We publish some of the world's most-read research, and we're now in a rare position: applying modern AI to a corpus of trusted scientific knowledge that spans two centuries. Researchers will use the systems you build here to move faster and get closer to the answers they came for. That's the work: from knowledge to impact.
We power infinite possibilities.
For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.
We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.
Here, your talent matters. Your ideas have room to grow. And your work creates breakthroughs that can change everything.

Performance modelling

Product testing & proving

Researching novel techniques for next generation communication systems

Electronic warfare
•
Missile survivability through stealth and electromagnetic modelling

Digital signal processing
•
Waveform design
•
Message protocols using the OSI model
•
Software defined radio

Excellent opportunities for personal development

Ability to apply technical knowledge to influence the direction of technologies and projects
•
Experience products at different phases of the product lifecycle

Diverse range of roles available creating varied and stimulating work

Interest in RF technologies

Location: Bristol, UK (Hybrid)
Hybrid Model: Office: Mon - Thurs, Fridays Remote
Our Team:
Semtech’s Signal Integrity Products group develops industry-leading high-speed semiconductor solutions that enable next-generation communications infrastructure across data centres, cloud computing, optical networking, and high-performance connectivity applications. Our advanced portfolio of optical and electrical products supports increasingly demanding bandwidth requirements, helping customers deliver faster, more reliable data transmission technologies worldwide.
As innovation in high-speed connectivity continues to accelerate, our engineering teams are focused on developing increasingly sophisticated products that push the boundaries of signal integrity performance. To support this continued growth, we are expanding our Characterization Engineering team in Bristol and seeking an experienced Senior Characterization Engineer to play a critical role in new product development and validation activities.
Job Summary:
As a Senior Characterization Engineer, you will be responsible for leading, planning, and executing bench PVT characterization activities for advanced high-speed signal integrity products across both optical and electrical semiconductor technologies.
Working as part of an international development team spanning the UK, Canada, the United States, and Mexico, you will develop automated test solutions, execute comprehensive characterization plans, analyze complex datasets, and collaborate closely with cross-functional engineering teams to ensure successful product development and release.
This position requires a highly motivated engineer who thrives in a laboratory environment, demonstrates strong technical ownership, and is comfortable working independently while contributing to a collaborative global engineering organization.
Responsibilities:
• Lead planning and execution of characterization activities for assigned New Product Introduction (NPI) products, including development of characterization plans, scheduling, equipment selection, hardware preparation, and fixture design. (30%)
• Develop and bring up robust, repeatable automated test environments while executing test plans and performing real-time analysis of characterization results to ensure accurate and timely project delivery. (25%)
• Generate complex datasets, produce detailed technical reports, review findings with cross-functional engineering teams, and proactively manage follow-up actions to maintain product quality and performance standards. (20%)
• Contribute to ongoing automation and process development activities, including Python-based test automation, automated test method development, signal integrity improvements, and implementation of AI tools to improve engineering efficiency. (15%)
• Support technical development within the wider engineering team by mentoring junior engineers, sharing technical expertise, and continuously expanding knowledge of emerging technologies, test equipment, standards, and advanced packaging technologies. (10%)
Minimum Qualifications:
• BEng or MEng in Electronic Engineering or closely related discipline
• 5–10 years of relevant industry experience in semiconductor, signal integrity, or high-speed electronics development environments
• Strong experience and understanding of signal integrity testing for high-speed analogue silicon products
• Hands-on experience developing automation solutions using Python or similar programming languages
• Strong understanding of PCB design fundamentals for high-frequency and high-speed data rate applications
• Experience working within laboratory environments using advanced electronic test equipment
• Proven ability to generate, manage, and analyze large and complex engineering datasets
• Excellent debugging, troubleshooting, and analytical problem-solving skills
Desired Qualifications
• Experience characterizing high-speed optical or electrical semiconductor products
• Strong understanding of high-frequency measurement techniques and signal integrity analysis methodologies
• Experience working with automated test equipment development and hardware integration
• Comfortable collaborating within global, cross-functional engineering teams across multiple international locations
• Strong technical communication skills with the ability to clearly present data and engineering findings
• High attention to detail with excellent organizational and execution skills under tight project schedules
• Experience identifying process improvement opportunities and driving automation efficiency initiatives
• Interest in applying AI-based tools to improve engineering workflows and productivity
Why Join Us?
• Work on cutting-edge high-speed semiconductor technologies that power next-generation global communications infrastructure
• Collaborate with highly skilled engineering teams across an international and multidisciplinary organization
• Take ownership of critical product characterization activities that directly influence product quality and successful product launch
• Join an engineering culture focused on innovation, technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Career Growth Philosophy:
At Semtech, we believe our greatest innovations come from empowering exceptional engineering talent. We are committed to supporting professional development through mentorship, continuous technical learning, and providing opportunities to work on highly complex, industry-leading technologies.
Our pay-for-performance culture recognizes technical excellence, initiative, and leadership contribution. Engineers within this role are encouraged to continuously develop new skills, expand their technical expertise, and play a key role in shaping both their own career development and the future of Semtech’s advanced semiconductor technologies.

The intent of this job description is to describe the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job.
Incumbents may be required to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically included in this description.
All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions and requirements and are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

At Nexperia Manchester, we are expanding our Applications team with the addition of a Senior Application Engineer. Our Power MOSFET groups supply high-quality devices to the automotive, industrial, computing, and consumer sectors, providing advanced solutions for the electrification of the automotive industry and the high-density power requirements of AI and data centre infrastructure.
We are looking for a Senior Application Engineer who is passionate about - and ideally experienced working on - AI infrastructure or Data Centre power systems. In return, we can offer you a place in a growing team, travel opportunities, huge scope to continue your development and make a real impact on a global semiconductor manufacturer producing over 100 billion devices every year.
What you will do
As a Senior Application Engineer, you will be jointly responsible for the development of high-reliability power protection solutions for AI and data centre server racks. You will build a solid understanding of next generation 48V power distribution architectures and partner with the data centre team to support new business development in the hyperscale computing market.
Duties will include:
• Designing, debugging, and validating hot-swap protection and eFuse implementations for high-density rack systems
• Performing detailed MOSFET Safe Operating Area (SOA) characterisation and thermal validation
• Creating technical literature, demo boards, and reference models for 48V power distribution systems
• Defining new product specifications based on customer inputs and market trends
• Providing expert technical support to global sales teams and customers to resolve complex power delivery challenges
What you will need
Essential
• A Degree or equivalent in Electronics Engineering, Physics, or a relevant discipline
• Passion and experience working on AI infrastructure or Data Centre power systems
• Proven expertise in circuit simulation (e.g. SIMPLIS, LTspice, PSpice etc) and PCB design.
• The legal right and willingness to travel globally, occasionally on short notice to key technology hubs (e.g. USA/Asia) without significant visa processing delays
Experience of the following would be beneficial
• Power electronics: 48V distribution, OR-ing FETs, Hot-Swap controllers, and high-current MOSFET switching
• Applications: Server Power Supplies (CRPS), AI Accelerators, and high-reliability rack protection
• Advanced Simulation: FEA, SPICE modelling (device level), and thermal analysis.
Interview process
Stage 1: Recruiter Review
Stage 2: 60‑minute Technical Interview
Stage 3: 60‑minute Competency Interview

Remuneration & Reward – Excellent salary DOE, Bonus up to 10% (stretch up to 20%), excellent contributory pension scheme of up to 9%, recognition rewards scheme, EV salary sacrifice scheme, income protection, 12 x salary life assurance policy.

The role is responsible for optimising production schedules to ensure products are manufactured and delivered on time while minimising waste and maximising operational efficiency.
Working closely with cross-functional teams across EMEA, the Production Planner ensures production activities align with business objectives and proactively manages any disruptions that could impact supply continuity.
Key Responsibilities
The Production Planner is responsible for creating and maintaining detailed production schedules that support business requirements and meet customer expectations. Working collaboratively with Sales, Production, Procurement, Exports, Supply Chain Planning, and other key stakeholders across the region, the role ensures that production plans are aligned with demand forecasts, inventory levels, and operational capabilities.
The role is responsible for developing and maintaining production plans and schedules that support customer demand and business objectives, whilst ensuring alignment of production activities with forecasted demand through close collaboration with Sales, Production, Procurement, Exports, and Supply Chain teams. The Production Planner monitors raw material and finished goods inventory levels, identifying potential shortages, excess stock, and supply risks, and utilises effective inventory, stock, and forecast management techniques to optimise working capital and maintain continuity of supply.
The position coordinates production adjustments and material procurement activities in response to changing business requirements and is responsible for identifying and resolving scheduling conflicts, capacity constraints, and production bottlenecks to support efficient manufacturing operations. The Production Planner manages production orders, material requirements, and inventory transactions within ERP/MRP systems, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of planning data at all times.
A key aspect of the role involves reviewing production performance, analysing key performance indicators (KPIs), and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement. Corrective actions are implemented where required to improve planning accuracy, service levels, inventory performance, and operational efficiency. The Production Planner also supports engineering change management activities, ensuring that product and process changes are effectively incorporated into production plans with minimal disruption, whilst supporting wider supply continuity initiatives across the EMEA region.
The role is responsible for preparing and delivering regular performance reports to management, highlighting achievements, risks, challenges, and proposed solutions. Compliance with month-end processes, inventory control procedures, company policies, quality standards, and health and safety requirements must be maintained at all times. In addition, the Production Planner is expected to continuously seek opportunities to improve planning processes, systems, reporting tools, and ways of working, while providing flexible support to other site functions during peak periods, holiday cover, business-critical activities, and periods of increased operational demand in order to meet business objectives.
Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate will typically possess a qualification in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline, together with a minimum of three to five years' experience in production planning, scheduling, or supply chain roles within a manufacturing environment.
They will have strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, capacity planning, production scheduling, and inventory management principles, together with experience working with ERP/MRP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards (JDE), or similar platforms. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are essential, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and make informed decisions.
The role requires excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the organisation. Candidates must possess strong organisational and time-management skills and be capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, is also required.
The successful individual will be able to work independently whilst collaborating effectively within cross-functional teams and will be expected to support other site functions during peak periods, holiday cover, business-critical activities, and periods of increased operational demand, providing flexible cross-functional support as required to meet business objectives.
Key Competencies
The successful Production Planner will demonstrate strong capability in production planning and scheduling, demand and forecast management, inventory optimisation, capacity planning, and supply chain coordination. They will possess a high level of competence in ERP/MRP systems management, data analysis and reporting, continuous improvement methodologies, problem solving, and decision making.
Success in the role will also require excellent stakeholder management, communication, and collaboration skills, together with the ability to build effective working relationships across functions and regions to support business objectives and operational performance.

leave during Christmas/New Year period.

You’ll also be a subject matter expert across the product suite, supporting post-implementation technical questions and contributing to pre-sales discussions.
You’ll work directly with customers’ clinical operations, data, and IT teams, and with our Product and Engineering teams, to turn customer needs into working solutions. You’ll stay close to products in development and translate their requirements into delivery approaches. Our product space is new, so this role suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, is energized by emerging technology, and is happy to roll up their sleeves to deliver digital health solutions at scale.
While this is a remote position, the role is customer-facing by design. You will be expected to travel on-site with customers as needed — particularly customer UAT and customer governance — building the relationships and trust that underpin successful delivery.
What You’ll Do
Lead customer data conversations
• Lead discovery with customers on data requirements, identifying the right datasets, data owners, and cross-functional stakeholders for each data type.
• Advise customers on data standards and on how their data maps to Evinova’s out-of-the-box offerings.
• Develop deep expertise in Evinova’s data landscape and in customer data architectures, providing technical oversight during implementation and configuration.
• Present clearly and confidently to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior customer stakeholders.
Technical implementation
• Guide customers through collecting source data specifications, preparing datasets, and mapping and transforming data to Evinova standards where needed.
• Support customer onboarding to ingest sponsor-specific data sources.
• Build and prepare data deliverables hands-on where needed, and load them into customer environments.
• Review customer-provided data for quality and completeness, and resolve issues before load.
• Validate loaded data in customer environments and reconcile it against source.
• Manage defects and issues through to resolution in partnership with Product and Engineering, and lead root-cause analysis and remediation.
• Navigate formal change control and environment promotion, coordinating approvals, dependencies, and timelines.
• Champion change initiatives using change-management best practices, aligning delivery with strategic goals, product releases, and cross-functional needs during complex transitions.
• Track and communicate implementation progress across customers and internal partners, working independently across multiple engagements and proactively identifying and mitigating risks.
Integrations
• Oversee end-to-end customer data integration, including gathering requirements, configuring, testing, and maintaining integrations, and troubleshooting connectivity issues.
• Manage configuration as code and coordinate reviews and approvals with Platform and Security partners.
• Support system-upgrade impact assessments and update integrations after implementation.
• Ensure data exchange meets applicable data privacy and regulatory requirements
Be the product SME
• Answer post-implementation technical and data questions and serve as an escalation point for data-related issues.
• Support pre-sales with technical and data questions, such as feasibility and scoping.
• Act as a key liaison between customers, internal teams, vendors, and our Product and Engineering teams, and work with Product to shape solutions and feed customer insights back into the roadmap.
• Establish and document best practices for data exchange, including monitoring and troubleshooting processes, and develop and optimize delivery playbooks, templates, and checklists that make use of Evinova’s automated tools.
• Train internal teams and customers on data exchange procedures and standards.
• Keep a commercial mindset, making sure integration and delivery work creates value for customers and for Evinova.
Essential Qualifications
• Previous demonstrated experience in clinical operations, clinical data management, clinical trial planning, or a related technical field where data informs study decisions.
• Strong working knowledge of clinical trial data structures, terminologies, and standards, including USDM and CDISC.
• Hands-on familiarity with clinical trial operational, study design, cost and rate, and feasibility data, ideally including both clinical operational data and cost or finance data.
• Strong background in the technical implementation of customer-facing data integrations across organizations, ideally for enterprise SaaS customers.
• Strong working skills with structured data formats and secure file transfer.
• Comfort with configuration in version control, command-line tools, and basic cloud concepts (for example, AWS).
• Experience with work-tracking and documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence.
• Demonstrated ability to analyze data flows, identify discrepancies, and troubleshoot complex data issues.
• Ability to manage high-visibility, technical customer engagements, work independently across multiple engagements, and own problems end to end.
• Executive presence and strong communication, with the ability to translate technical topics for non-technical audiences and collaborate across diverse teams.
• Highly organized and solution-oriented, with resilience and adaptability in a fast-moving, newly emerging product space, and a passion for improving healthcare through technology.
